# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working group focused on governance frameworks, risk management strategies, and regulatory compliance considerations for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a].

# Operations
The working group maintains standardized meeting templates and agent-assisted workflows to document proceedings, record decisions, and track action items and deliverables[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee (TC)
proposed_concept.description: The body responsible for reviewing project proposals, recommending projects, and applying the Project Lifecycle Policy for the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) assists the Governing Board (GB) of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) by reviewing new project proposals, recommending projects that align with the AAIF mission, and applying the Project Lifecycle Policy (the “Lifecycle Policy”) to Technical Projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Architecture / Specification
The TC is composed of one representative appointed by each Platinum Member of AAIF [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

Key responsibilities include [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
1. Establishing, managing, and archiving Working Groups (WGs) enabling collaboration on matters in domains relevant to the scope of the AAIF.
2. Coordinating collaboration between Technical Projects, including the development of overall technical priorities and a vision for the community.
3. Recommending projects to the GB for acceptance as Technical Projects.
4. Deciding changes in a Technical Project’s status within the Lifecycle Policy.
5. Electing a TC Chair and optionally a Co-Chair annually.
6. Applying and maintaining the Lifecycle Policy, subject to GB approval.

Decisions are generally consensus-based. If voting is required, it is one-vote-per-voting-member. Quorum requires 50% of voting members. Decisions can be made via lazy consensus, where a proposal is automatically approved if no formal objection from a TC voting member is recorded within 72 hours [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History
The TC Charter was adopted on March 3, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group (GRR WG) focuses on establishing frameworks, risk assessment protocols, and guidance for regulatory compliance concerning agentic AI [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. The WG operates on a biweekly cadence, using a shared Google Doc as the primary collaboration artifact [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Architecture / Specification
The WG adopted a three-step working model for its deliverables [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:
1. Landscape analysis of existing standards, frameworks, and regulations (e.g., EU AI Act and eIDAS 2 [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]).
2. Gap analysis identifying where current approaches fail to address emerging agentic AI risks.
3. Distilled guidance/principles for organizations (pending scope decision on implementation guidance).

Initial deliverables include a draft charter, problem set statements, landscape inputs, and candidate risk-assessment/protocol concepts for agent-human oversight interactions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f], [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]. The WG maintains a focus on pre-competitive outputs that map existing work before proposing new guidance [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

# Lifecycle History
The WG held its kickoff meeting on 2026-02-19 [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
The WG adopted its three-step deliverable model on 2026-03-05 [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent observability, session-level trace models, and alignment across ecosystem standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish a shared understanding of AI agent observability and trace telemetry.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

# Architecture / Specification

Rather than serving as a competing standards body, the working group operates as a coordination forum interfacing with upstream standards such as OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

Key focus areas include:
- Addressing fragmentation across proprietary and open agent observability platforms.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- Bridging the gap between single LLM call tracing and session- or workflow-level agent behavior across multi-turn tool invocations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]
- Tracing content lineage, fidelity, and grounding across multi-modal agent workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

# Lifecycle History

The working group charter was drafted under the primary leadership of Pavan Sudheendra.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]

proposed_concept.title: Case Study Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Guidelines and qualification criteria for AAIF member organizations submitting written and webinar implementation case studies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation publishes case studies showcasing member organization implementations of open agentic standards such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, and AGENTS.md to resolve production challenges.[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]

# Architecture / Specification

Case studies are accepted in two primary formats:
- **Written Case Study**: Open to member organizations highlighting direct or customer implementations that deliver verifiable business impact.[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]
- **Webinar Case Study**: Recorded 20–30 minute presentations with Q&A distributed across AAIF media channels.[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]

Submissions are prioritized based on agentic maturity (advancing beyond simple chatbots to autonomous systems), cross-framework interoperability, and quantitative proof of acceleration or error reduction.[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]

# Overview
The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape provides a view into the overall agentic AI ecosystem, categorizing prominent open source software and open standards projects, alongside AAIF members and projects [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

The landscape is generated using data files from the `aaif/aaif-landscape` repository, utilizing the `cncf/landscape2` software [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Lifecycle History
The landscape is generated daily, meaning changes merged into the source repository should be visible within 24 hours [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# References
The landscape is publicly available at `https://landscape.aaif.io` [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Agentic AI Landscape Inclusion Criteria
proposed_concept.description: Rules governing which projects, organizations, and software are eligible for inclusion in the AAIF Agentic AI Landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
To be included in the AAIF Agentic AI Landscape, entries must adhere to specific guidelines primarily focused on open source status, community adoption, and relevance to agentic AI [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Architecture / Specification
Key inclusion criteria include:
1. Open source projects generally require at least 1000 GitHub stars and must clearly fit into an existing category.
2. Organizations are generally limited to listing only one major or best-known project.
3. Commercial versions of open source software, closed source products, services, or proprietary standards are not included.
4. Entries require a logo in SVG format, which must include the name in English, and should avoid reversed or overly horizontal layouts.
5. The Crunchbase organization listed should be the entity controlling the software, typically the trademark owner [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

Submissions are made via pull request to the `landscape.yml` file in the `aaif/aaif-landscape` repository, with the logo added to the `hosted_logos` directory [^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.title: Code of Conduct
proposed_concept.description: Code of conduct governing participation across Agentic AI Foundation committees, working groups, events, and community spaces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Code of Conduct establishes community standards and rules of engagement across all Foundation activities [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]. The Foundation pledges to foster an inclusive, welcoming, and harassment-free environment for all participants regardless of personal background or identity [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope
The Code of Conduct applies across AAIF governance and community interactions [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588]:
- Governing Board meetings
- Technical Committee meetings (see [Technical Committee](technical-committee.md))
- Working Group meetings
- Outreach Committee and other AAIF committee meetings
- General Foundation communications, channels, and social media activities

## Inter-Policy Relationships
- **Foundation Events**: Events produced by the AAIF with professional events staff are governed by the Linux Foundation Events Code of Conduct in conjunction with this Code of Conduct [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].
- **Umbrella Technical Projects**: Technical projects supported by the AAIF operate as distinct projects and maintain their own codes of conduct [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

## Behavioral Standards
- **Expected Behavior**: Community members must use welcoming language, respect alternative perspectives, accept constructive feedback, prioritize community benefit, and collaborate responsibly [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].
- **Unacceptable Behavior**: Harassment, discrimination, intimidation, sustained disruption, sexualized or threatening language, personal attacks, and unauthorized sharing of private information are prohibited [^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Design and editorial guidelines defining AAIF's neutral, collaborative, and trustworthy brand identity.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines define the visual, editorial, and design standards for all Agentic AI Foundation deliverables, presentations, websites, documents, diagrams, and marketing assets [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]. The brand identity is built to convey vendor neutrality, collective ecosystem ownership, and Linux Foundation-backed credibility [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

# Architecture / Specification
## Core Brand Pillars
- **Neutral**: Governance designed so no single vendor dominates the ecosystem. Materials avoid single-vendor visual dominance, unbalanced layouts, or hype-driven winner-takes-all narratives [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].
- **Collaborative**: Emphasizes cross-industry cooperation and shared open standards using inclusive framing (such as "collective" and "open ecosystem") rather than hero-centric framing [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].
- **Trustworthy**: Grounded in the Linux Foundation's governance track record. Communications favor precise claims, high-contrast typography, and clean compositions over chaotic or speculative AI aesthetic trends [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

## Color Palette
- **Primary Palette**: White (`#ffffff`) and Black (`#000000`) for high-contrast, clean foundational compositions [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

## Agent Skill Integration
The guidelines are also published as a reusable Agent Skill in the [Public Agents](../project/public-agents.md) repository (`skills/aaif-brand-guidelines`) for automated brand compliance across AI agent workflows [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b, ^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

proposed_concept.title: Public Agents Skills Repository
proposed_concept.description: A repository of portable Agent Skills providing reusable instructions, assets, and workflows for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Public Agents repository (`aaif/public-agents`) distributes portable Agent Skills that provide AI agents with reusable domain expertise, brand instructions, references, and executable workflows [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]. Skills are designed to be context-loaded on demand by major AI agent runtimes [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

# Architecture / Specification
## Repository and Skill Structure
Skills in the repository follow the Agent Skills specification [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]:
- `SKILL.md`: Required YAML frontmatter metadata (`name`, `description`, `author`, `organization`, `version`) followed by Markdown instructions [^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b, ^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `assets/`: Supporting visual assets, templates, and logos [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `references/`: Extended reference materials and documentation [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `scripts/`: Executable helper scripts [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

## Management and Integration
Skills can be installed, updated, and listed via the Skills CLI (`npx skills`) [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]. Installed skills are automatically loaded by compatible AI agents (including Goose, Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini) based on prompt context [^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

proposed_concept.title: Public Agents
proposed_concept.description: A repository of public, reusable agent resources including Agent Skills, recipes, prompts, and model testing workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Public Agents is an AAIF repository providing reusable agent assets, instructions, recipes, and automation workflows for agentic AI development.[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7] It houses modular capabilities such as domain expertise guidelines, repeatable multi-step recipes, and prompt templates, alongside testing workflows for multi-provider LLM integrations.[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]

# Architecture / Specification
The repository organizes agent resources across dedicated functional directories:[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]
- `skills/`: Agent Skills containing reusable domain expertise, brand guidance (such as the AAIF brand guidelines skill), workflows, and tool-specific instructions.[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7][^evt-public-agents-pr-1]
- `recipes/`: Repeatable task workflows and operational definitions for agent execution.[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]
- `prompts/`: Reusable prompt collections and structured prompt templates.[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]
- `docs/`: Supporting documentation for contributors and adopters.[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]

# Workflows and Model Integration
Public Agents provides GitHub Actions testing workflows for executing inference calls against external model providers:[^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]
- **`copilot-test-action`**: Queries the GitHub Models catalog endpoint (`https://models.github.ai/catalog/models`) and executes chat completion inference requests against org-scoped endpoints using repository `GITHUB_TOKEN` credentials.[^evt-public-agents-file-b248ae41d1f0-0667ce2f]
- **`gemini-test-action`**: Dispatches generation requests directly to Google Gemini API endpoints using a configured `GEMINI_API_KEY` secret passed via HTTP headers.[^evt-public-agents-file-ae1d68d00103-0e76c626]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security and privacy threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, and cross-ecosystem protocol alignment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) develops security threat models, privacy frameworks, and best practices across the agentic AI landscape.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5] The working group coordinates cross-foundation alignment on agentic taxonomies and tracks protocol extensions impacting agent security boundaries.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]

# Architecture / Specification
Key focus areas and operational initiatives within the working group include:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy Collaboration**: Serving as the initial cross-working-group initiative across AAIF, utilizing the SP WG draft taxonomy as the baseline to unify definitions across working groups before formalizing landscape terminology.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]
- **Protocol Security and Integrations**: Tracking external protocol developments, including Model Context Protocol (MCP) Interceptors for data privacy and redaction hooks, and MCP Apps UI boundary security.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]
- **Workstream Structure**: Evolving bi-weekly all-hands meetings into checkpoint meetings while organizing self-directed, asynchronous workstreams around specific deliverables.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]

# Lifecycle History
The SP WG charter was submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in April 2026; following initial approvals and absence of substantive objections, the working group initiated operational workstreams and cross-WG taxonomy alignment.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group addressing agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and cross-organizational trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust (I&T) Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation working group established to define and promote vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Its goal is to enable agents to be discovered across platforms, prove who they are and who they act for, verify human approvals, and operate securely across systems and organizational boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope
The working group focuses on several core areas across enterprise and consumer contexts[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: How agents authenticate, convey operational provenance, and establish their origin context.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: How agents represent delegated authority on behalf of humans, teams, roles, or automated processes.
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained authorization patterns, policy constraints, and human approval or governance controls.
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: How systems evaluate whether to trust external agents and verify permissions for requested actions.
- **Agent Discovery and Trust-Relevant Metadata**: Describing and discovering agents to facilitate interoperability, observability, and traceability.

## Boundaries and Coordination
The group coordinates across the foundation while observing clear boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- Comprehensive agent security controls and execution architectures are primarily handled by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- The group does not act as a formal standards development organization (SDO) to ratify standards independently, but informs and contributes recommendations to standards bodies[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].
- Metadata and discovery representations align with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Blog Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial policies, contributor eligibility criteria, and submission workflow for publishing on the Agentic AI Foundation blog.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) blog serves as a central hub for publishing technical insights, open source project updates, community milestones, and deployment case studies across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]. Publishing on aaif.io is managed end-to-end by the Linux Foundation team, with an intake process open to member companies, project maintainers, working groups, and community contributors[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification
## Contributor Eligibility and Frequency
- **Member Companies:** Content must remain vendor-neutral and mission-aligned, permitting at most two closing sentences with a single external link[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Project Maintainers & Contributors:** Focuses on release notes, roadmaps, and technical deep-dives for hosted projects such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, and AGENTS.md[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Working Groups & Technical Committee:** Authored directly by working groups or the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`)[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Community Contributors:** Submissions covering tutorials and ecosystem thought leadership are capped at two posts per month per author[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

## Content Requirements
Submissions require a standard two-week lead time and must satisfy specific criteria[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]:
- **Originality & Timeliness:** Content must be previously unpublished and reflect activity from the preceding two months[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Neutrality:** Strictly vendor-neutral narrative without sales pitches, promotional framing, or criticism of open source projects[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Format:** Narrative article format ranging between 600 and 1,500 words[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed].
- **Automation Tooling:** Contributors can use the `aaif-blog-guidelines` skill distributed through `../project/public-agents.md` to format and check drafts[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent observability, session-level trace models, and alignment across ecosystem telemetry standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group established to foster a shared understanding of agent observability and telemetry standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. The group was ratified on April 15, 2026, approved on May 13, 2026, and is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification
## Mission and Principles
OT-WG operates primarily as a coordination forum rather than a competing standards body[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]. It bridges fragmented telemetry practices across proprietary platforms and aligns with external standards initiatives like OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

Key guiding principles include:
- **Coordinate First:** Align with and contribute upstream to existing standards bodies before defining new specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Interoperability over Innovation:** Emphasize composability with established open telemetry standards[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Observable by Default:** Ensure agent systems provide out-of-the-box visibility into multi-turn execution, tool invocation, and decision state[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].
- **Neutrality:** Maintain framework and vendor neutrality across all deliverables[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

## Focus Area Model
The WG organizes technical output into focus areas and focus groups, starting with the founding Agent Behavior Trace Model to extend telemetry beyond single LLM calls to workflow- and session-level multi-modal interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, security taxonomies, and privacy design patterns for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes security and data protection as a core shared discipline across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899]. Approved on May 13, 2026, and chaired by Alex Frazer, the group develops open threat models, taxonomies, and architectural patterns for trustworthy agentic systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification
## Mandate and Scope
SPAA addresses unique agentic vulnerabilities such as prompt injection, confused deputy issues, authorization boundary failures, tool execution hazards, and agent memory integrity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

In-scope activities include:
- Threat modeling and adversarial attack analysis[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Security architecture and containment design patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Privacy engineering and data lifecycle protection across autonomous workflows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Cross-group collaboration with peer bodies including `../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md` and `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

## Out of Scope Boundaries
To maintain technical focus, SPAA explicitly excludes:
- Normative ethics, bias, and value judgements (deferred to Governance and Policy groups)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Regulatory interpretation and prescriptive compliance certification[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- Formal certification programs for agentic tools or platforms[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (S&P WG) is an AAIF working group dedicated to defining cross-ecosystem security architectures, threat models, and privacy design patterns for agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. It provides guidance on multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation security, delegated authorization, agent memory protection, and containment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

Leadership of the working group includes Chair Alex Frazer and Co-Chair Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. The group coordinates closely with adjacent standards efforts including Model Context Protocol (MCP) working groups and the Agentic AI Risk Model (AARM) initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope

- **In-Scope:** Threat modeling, security architecture, agent control and containment mechanisms, data protection, and cross-working-group security review checklists [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].
- **Out-of-Scope:** Subjective ethics and bias interpretations, formal regulatory compliance certification, and legal counsel [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

## Deliverables and Workstreams

1. **Taxonomy:** Originally seeded within the WG and subsequently elevated to an AAIF-wide cross-WG initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
2. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Near-term assessment analyzing tool invocation risks, cascading failures, prompt injection, and goal drift [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
3. **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** A lightweight checklist for other AAIF working groups such as `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md` and `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` to self-audit deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
4. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Technical implementation patterns including execution hooks, sandboxing checkpoints, and human-in-the-loop controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
5. **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide:** High-level operational guidance pairing with the design patterns catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History

- **Initial Charter Draft:** Initial charter authored under PR #1, defining the governance structure, scope boundaries, and meeting cadences [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].
- **Charter Approval and LFX Transition:** Formal approval transitioned to the Linux Foundation LFX platform vote [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Overview
The AAIF Landscape is an interactive architectural and ecosystem map tracking agent runtimes, protocols, security guardrails, observability platforms, commerce rails, and regulatory regimes across the agentic AI domain[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]. It visualizes foundation members, hosted projects, and the broader open source ecosystem using categorized groupings and project tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is built on CNCF Landscape 2 tooling and maintained with automated validation and pull request preview workflows[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007][^evt-aaif-landscape-file-a5c0f08bc43f-3b9f2340][^evt-aaif-landscape-file-16e486445ce2-29580b00].

## Project Tiers
Entries in the landscape are categorized across defined tiers[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007]:
- **Graduated**: Mature projects meeting full governance and adoption criteria[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Incubating**: Active projects progressing toward maturity and sustainability[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **Member**: Projects and assets associated with AAIF member organizations[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].
- **External**: Ecosystem software and tooling maintained outside AAIF governance[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-50664ea2b31a-0cc09007].

## Watchlist and Ecosystem Tracking
The landscape includes a project watchlist highlighting leading agentic AI open source software, designed to sync with the Agentic AI Momentum Dashboard on LFX Insights[^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-14]. Eligibility for entries follows the rules outlined in the [Landscape Inclusion Criteria](../guidelines/landscape-inclusion-criteria.md).

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Guidelines detailing the process, requirements, and evaluation criteria for proposing new Working Groups within the AAIF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation welcomes proposals for new Working Groups (WGs) from its members. Working Groups are the primary mechanism through which the Foundation advances research, develops standards, and produces actionable guidance on topics critical to the responsible development and deployment of agentic AI systems [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

A Working Group is a structured, time-bound collaboration of subject matter experts convened to address a specific challenge, produce defined deliverables, or advance a particular area of work relevant to the Foundation's mission. WGs may focus on technical, policy, governance, safety, or cross-cutting themes within the agentic AI landscape [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Submission Requirements

Submissions are open only to Foundation Members (member organizations in good standing from any level membership) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

To be considered, a proposal must include the following eight elements:

1.  **Submitter Information**: Full name, organizational affiliation, role, contact email, and indication of willingness/capacity to help lead.
2.  **Working Group Identity**: A clear, concise name and a one-sentence summary of the group's focus, avoiding jargon.
3.  **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Clear articulation of the challenge, gap, or opportunity being addressed, its relevance to agentic AI, and alignment with the Foundation's mission.
4.  **Proposed Scope & Deliverables**: Definition of the intended scope of work, key topics, and expected outputs. Deliverables may include technical reports, frameworks, standards, datasets, benchmarks, tooling, or policy recommendations.
5.  **Timeline & Structure**: Proposed timeline, expected meeting cadence, and suggested duration (most WGs operate on a 12–24 month charter cycle).
6.  **Membership & Expertise**: Identification of needed expertise and stakeholder perspectives, including any individuals or organizations who have already expressed interest.
7.  **Impact & Urgency**: Justification for the work.
8.  **Resource Considerations**: Any necessary resources or infrastructure [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Evaluation Criteria

Proposals are evaluated based on: alignment with the AAIF mission, clarity of scope and deliverables, feasibility, community interest, and potential impact [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Policy defining the process for projects to join the AAIF, including proposal requirements, acceptance stages, and annual review criteria.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Lifecycle Policy describes how an open technical project can formally join the Agentic AI Foundation (“AAIF”) via the Project Proposal Process. It defines the Stages a project may be admitted to, the criteria and expectations for each stage, and the acceptance criteria for movement between stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

## Project Proposal Process

The proposal process is the same for existing projects seeking to move into the AAIF and for new projects to be formed within the AAIF. Submissions must be made through the AAIF project proposals GitHub repository [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

Required information for a project submission includes:
*   Project name, description, origin, and history.
*   Statement on alignment with the AAIF mission and relation to existing AAIF projects.
*   Example use cases and evidence of adoption.
*   Sponsor from the [../governance/technical-committee.md](Technical Committee), if identified.
*   OSI-approved permissive license under which the project is released.
*   Location of the public repository.
*   Automated validation/release processes, release methodology, and public-facing contribution process.
*   Publicly accessible issue tracker and external project dependencies.
*   Names of project core maintainers, description of the leadership team and decision-making process, and documented governance practices (e.g., `GOVERNANCE.md`).
*   List of official communication channels, website link, and social media accounts.
*   Details of existing financial sponsorship and infrastructure needs [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

## Stages: Definitions and Expectations

Projects progress through stages based on maturity and community adoption.

### Growth Stage
This stage is for projects that are early in their lifecycle, focusing on establishing a community, defining scope, and achieving initial adoption. Expectations include having a clear mission, an active maintainer team, and adherence to AAIF governance policies. Acceptance criteria focus on demonstrating community interest and technical viability [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

### Impact Stage
This stage is for projects that have demonstrated significant growth, stability, and broad adoption. Expectations include having a diverse contributor base, clear governance, and production readiness. Acceptance criteria require demonstrating substantial community engagement, clear metrics, and alignment with industry needs [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

### Emeritus Stage
This stage is for projects that are no longer actively maintained or have reached end-of-life. Projects in this stage have little to no activity and are preserved for historical reference or potential future revival [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171] [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

proposed_concept.title: Social Media Governance and Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Policies governing the content strategy, tone, submission process, and usage guidelines for official Agentic AI Foundation social media channels.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Linux Foundation leads the Agentic AI Foundation social media content strategy, access, and compliance. Content is published and approved by Foundation staff to ensure consistency, accuracy, and alignment with project goals. The platforms are used to share Foundation-wide updates, including releases, milestones, events, and initiatives [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

## Tone and Content

The required tone is neutral, professional, inclusive, and clear, built to serve a global AI and developer audience.

**What is posted:**
*   Official releases and large milestones.
*   Foundation-led events, initiatives, and community calls.
*   Ecosystem tools or content featured in official project work [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

## Usage Guidelines

### Social Posts Baseline
Content must be relevant to agentic AI, inclusive, and avoid unsolicited promotions. Proper attribution must be given when sharing code or ideas. Platform-specific etiquette is maintained for X (short, engaging), LinkedIn (professional tone), and Bluesky (casual and conversational) [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

### Reposting Policy
The official AAIF channels will repost content that is:
*   Tied to official project releases.
*   Shared by core contributors or working groups to announce project changes.
*   Connected to official Foundation events or initiatives.

The Foundation will *not* repost personal blogs, code tips, videos, vendor products, or product announcements. Community projects are featured only when they explicitly showcase the implementation of AAIF standards (e.g., MCP, goose) [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications for commerce workflows carried out by AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) was approved on 2026-05-15 [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

## Mission

The AC WG advances the AAIF mission by cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows carried out by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems. The WG provides interoperability guidance and reference architectures across discovery, negotiation, checkout, payment orchestration, and post-purchase lifecycle interactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

The WG exists to address the lack of shared vocabulary and reference models across emerging protocols, fragmented interfaces across commerce systems, and insufficient shared guidance for trust, safety, and accountability in agent-initiated commerce. The WG does not author competing commerce protocols; it identifies common ground across existing and emerging work and recommends paths forward to the [../governance/technical-committee.md](Technical Committee) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

## Architecture / Specification

The WG focuses on **interfaces, signals, and interoperability patterns** between agentic systems and the broader commerce stack.

### In Scope
The scope covers the agentic commerce lifecycle, including:
*   **Discovery & negotiation**: Agent–merchant interfaces for offers, availability, and terms.
*   **Cart & checkout**: Composition, validation, and checkout handoff.
*   **Identity & delegated authority**: Buyer identity, agent authority scoping, and consent conveyance (in collaboration with the [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](Identity & Trust WG)).
*   **Agentic payments**: Interfaces between agents, wallets, and payment networks (intent, authorization, settlement signals).
*   **Fraud signaling**: Risk-posture signals exchanged between agents, merchants, and risk systems.
*   **Human-in-the-loop & autonomy boundaries**: Confirmation, escalation, and autonomy-level representation.
*   **Post-purchase interfaces**: Claims, dispute initiation, chargeback signaling, and order-status conveyance [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

### Out of Scope
The WG explicitly excludes:
*   Operations, internals, and implementation details of specific commerce systems (e.g., payment rail operations, fraud detection internals).
*   Responsible AI and societal-impact policy (handled at the Foundation level).
*   End-user UI, marketplace product design, and hardware.
*   Non-agentic commerce governance.
*   Authoring new commerce protocols [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

## Deliverables

Initial planned deliverables include:
1.  **Agentic Commerce Terminology and Reference Model**: A shared vocabulary and conceptual model for agentic commerce interactions.
2.  **Interoperability Guidance for Agent-Initiated Payments**: Best practices and patterns for agents interacting with payment systems.
3.  **Reference Architecture for Delegated Authority**: Guidance on how agents receive and exercise authority on behalf of users [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working group tasked with developing open threat models, security taxonomies, architectural control frameworks, and privacy guidelines across the agentic ecosystem.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its efforts across several key deliverable workstreams:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Developing threat models and security gap analyses, coordinated closely with cross-working-group taxonomy efforts.
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive recommendations for securing agent deployments, execution environments, and tool integrations.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural and implementation patterns addressing agent-specific vulnerabilities and risks.
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Baseline criteria used to review specifications and proposals from other AAIF working groups.
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Collaboration**: Joint leadership in the cross-WG Taxonomy workstream and Landscape workstream, co-chaired by Junjie Bu to survey ecosystem tooling with a security and privacy lens.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

# Lifecycle History

As of May 2026, the working group charter has received formal approval.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9] Workstreams operate with self-selected leads and contributor channels, coordinating async contributions via GitHub pull requests and bi-weekly synchronization meetings.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]

proposed_concept.description: Intake process, review criteria, graduation stages, and voting rules for open source projects applying to join the AAIF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Lifecycle governs how open source projects apply for, transition through, and maintain foundation-hosted status within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

# Architecture / Specification

## Intake and Review Process

1. **Proposal Submission**: Project maintainers submit an application via the standard proposal issue template in the `aaif/project-proposals` repository.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
2. **Triage and Presentation**: Applications are logged on the Project Proposals Board. Maintainers collaborate with AAIF staff to prepare a review presentation.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
3. **Technical Committee Review**: Proposals are reviewed during scheduled meetings of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), which classifies accepted projects as either **Growth** or **Impact** projects.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
4. **Voting and Approval**: Acceptance requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all Technical Committee members, followed by final referral and approval by the Governing Board.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

## Proposal Status Labels

- `New`: The proposal is submitted and placed in the review backlog.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Approved`: The application has been accepted into the foundation-hosted structure.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Declined`: The application was rejected, with explanations documented on the issue.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Waiting on Comment`: Additional information is required from applicants.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- `Too Early`: The project is not yet mature enough; guidance is provided for future submission.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

## Reapplication and Membership Rules

- **Reapplication**: Projects that are declined may reapply as soon as three months after a vote if tangible progress has been made.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]
- **Membership Neutrality**: Contributing projects do not need to originate from AAIF member organizations, nor does hosting acceptance grant member tiers or governing board seats to contributors.[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem map and taxonomy maintained under `ws-taxonomy-landscape` to categorize projects, runtimes, protocols, and developer tooling across the open agent ecosystem.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape organizes technologies into seven core functional categories, aligned directly with AAIF working groups:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]

1. **Agent Runtimes, Frameworks & Workflow Orchestration**: Autonomous agent frameworks and orchestration runtimes (aligned with Workflows & Process Integration and [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)).
2. **Protocols & Discovery Registries**: Discovery, delegation, and trust anchors (aligned with [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)).
3. **Security Guardrails & Firewalls**: Defensive layers and containment controls (aligned with [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)).
4. **Observability & Tracing Telemetry**: Agent-level tracing and telemetry platforms (aligned with [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)).
5. **Agentic Commerce & Wallets**: Agent payment rails and transaction infrastructure (aligned with [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md)).
6. **Global Governance & Regulatory Regimes**: Compliance frameworks and policy tooling (aligned with [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)).
7. **Agent Evaluation & Benchmarking Harnesses**: Evaluation suites and reliability harnesses (aligned with [Accuracy & Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md)).

# Governance and Maintenance

The landscape is maintained as a cross-working-group effort led by the Landscape and Taxonomy workstream chairs, with contributions managed through pull requests adhering to landscape inclusion criteria.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-182f41e6079f-9b5a15a8]

proposed_concept.description: Intake process, review criteria, status lifecycle, and voting rules for proposing new Working Groups within the Agentic AI Foundation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Submission Guidelines govern the formation of new Working Groups (WGs) within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Proposals are tracked publicly, reviewed by the Technical Committee (TC), and require both Technical Committee and Governing Board approval to launch.

# Architecture / Specification
## Application and Intake Workflow
1. **Submission**: Proposers open a Working Group Proposal Application issue on GitHub using the standardized issue template [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
2. **Tracking**: New submissions are added to the backlog on the Working Group Proposals project board for triage [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
3. **Review**: Proposals are scheduled for evaluation during upcoming [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) meetings [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Status Lifecycle Labels
- `New`: The proposal is newly submitted and queued in the backlog [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have requested clarifications or additional details via issue comments [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Too Early`: The proposal is deemed premature, with guidance provided for future reapplication [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Declined`: The proposal has been rejected, with rationale documented in comments [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
- `Approved`: The proposal has been accepted [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Voting and Approval Thresholds
To be accepted, a working group proposal must receive a simple majority vote of all members of the Technical Committee and remains subject to final approval by the AAIF Governing Board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) acts as a bridge between global AI policy frameworks and technical implementations across agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]. Led by Ryan Hagemann, the group addresses the absence of cohesive regulatory guidance and novel risk management mechanisms for autonomous agent architectures.

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope of Work
### In-Scope Areas
- **Policy Tracking**: Identifying, tracking, and monitoring international AI regulations, standards, and policy frameworks affecting autonomous agents [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- **Protocol Governance**: Analyzing how interoperability protocols (such as Model Context Protocol) are implemented within organizational governance boundaries [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- **Agent BoM & Provenance**: Formulating AI Agent Bill of Materials standards across foundation models, scaffolding, tools, APIs, and dependencies [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- **Reversibility Infrastructure**: Researching formal methods and protocols for action reversibility and undo infrastructures in agent workflows [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- **Autonomy & Oversight**: Defining Human-in-the-Loop patterns, autonomy tiers, deployment risk classifications, and incident reporting mechanisms [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

### Out-of-Scope
- Providing formal legal advice or individual compliance certifications [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].
- Endorsing specific commercial products or proprietary compliance solutions [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting Process
proposed_concept.description: Standardized monthly reporting cadence, pull request workflow, and template structure for AAIF working groups and workstreams reporting to the Technical Committee.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Working Group Reporting Process defines the cadence, submission format, and review procedure by which Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working groups and workstreams communicate progress, blockers, and required decisions to the Technical Committee (TC)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. Each active group submits monthly status updates via pull request to ensure open governance and asynchronous oversight[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Reporting Timeline and Cadence
Working groups and workstreams adhere to a uniform monthly reporting schedule[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23]:
- **Submission Deadline:** Reports are due by the last business day of the reporting month[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-9677055e316b-dc950981].
- **Review Window:** The [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) review window closes 7 calendar days after submission[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].
- **Merge Condition:** The report pull request is merged once the TC signs off or the 7-day review window closes, whichever is sooner[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

## Submission Workflow
1. Working group leadership copies `reporting/TEMPLATE.md` to `reporting/YYYY-MM-report.md` (e.g., `reporting/2026-06-report.md`)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
2. A pull request is submitted against the group's repository titled `[Report] <WG name> – <Month YYYY>`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a].
3. The TC (or its designated GitHub team) is assigned as reviewers for asynchronous assessment[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].

## Required Report Sections
Reports must remain short, scannable, and structured using the following sections[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]:
- **Summary:** A 2–3 sentence overview capturing the month at a glance.
- **Progress Against Objectives:** Shipped work and advancements tied to stated working group objectives.
- **Blockers and Risks:** Issues or impediments escalated for TC awareness.
- **Decisions Needed from the TC:** Explicit, actionable requests for TC decision-making.
- **Next Month's Focus:** Top 2–3 priorities for the coming month.
- **Metrics / Links:** Relevant pull requests, issues, releases, meeting notes, and dashboards.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops open threat models, security taxonomies, control frameworks, and privacy standards to protect agentic systems against adversarial exploits, data leakage, and unintended agent behavior.

# Architecture / Specification

## Deliverable Lifecycle

Deliverables produced by the working group follow a formal multi-stage lifecycle[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:
- **Draft**: Work in progress using the `DRAFT-` filename prefix (e.g., `DRAFT-taxonomy.md`)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Final**: Formally approved deliverables where the `DRAFT-` prefix is removed. Transition to Final requires explicit recorded approval in the Decisions section of a working group meeting note[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Moved**: Deliverables handed off to cross-WG workstreams or external repositories, maintained as redirects to preserve link integrity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].

## Repository Governance

The repository is divided into `charter/`, `deliverables/`, and `meeting-notes/`, each governed by dedicated instructions[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]. Charters remain in `charter/DRAFT.md` until formally approved by a recorded meeting decision[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]. Meeting notes follow a standardized template capturing discussion topics, decisions, and action items[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31].

# Proposals Under Review

External community proposals under active consideration include cross-referencing the draft taxonomy with OWASP Agentic Systems Incidents (ASI01-09) vectors, defining static analysis practices distinct from red teaming, and formalizing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) design patterns on consumer messaging surfaces[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-6].

# References

- [Repository Instructions](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/3a3d0ef5367e0beb6aafa56908ae277a73f133e0/AGENTS.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a54ff182c7e8-57e8a423]

- [Meeting Notes Workflow](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy/blob/3a3d0ef5367e0beb6aafa56908ae277a73f133e0/meeting-notes/AGENTS.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-eb9c68e792e7-3538ca31]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) establishes open threat models, security taxonomies, control frameworks, and privacy best practices for agentic AI systems. The WG operates through several focused workstreams to produce actionable guidance and specifications.

# Architecture / Specification
The SP WG currently focuses on the following workstreams:
1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Evaluating existing AI threat models against agentic-specific threats (e.g., multi-agent persuasion, delegated authorization) to determine if a new framework is warranted [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].
2. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Curating reusable design patterns for building secure and privacy-respecting agentic AI systems, documented in a problem/context/solution format [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].
3. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Providing practical, higher-level guidance for builders, including secrets management, secure tool invocation, and guardrails [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].
4. **Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist:** Defining a lightweight process for reviewing deliverables from other AAIF working groups (such as ../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md, ../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md, and ../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) through a security and privacy lens [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Lifecycle History
The initial workstream focused on a Taxonomy of Terms and Definitions was moved to the cross-WG AAIF Taxonomy / Landscape effort, where it is maintained as an AAIF-wide initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

proposed_concept.description: Evaluating existing AI threat model frameworks against agentic-specific threats to determine if a new framework is necessary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
This workstream evaluates existing AI threat model frameworks (such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) to determine if they adequately address threats specific to agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

# Architecture / Specification
The scope of analysis includes agentic-specific threats such as multi-agent persuasion, risks associated with tool invocation, delegated authorization boundaries, and supply-chain integrity (including system prompt integrity, model provenance, and tools manifest verification).

The primary output is a gap analysis and guidance document that establishes whether sufficient models exist or if agentic-specific gaps warrant new framework development. This output feeds into the downstream Design Patterns Catalog and Best Practices Guide workstreams (see ../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).

# Leads
The workstream is led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog
proposed_concept.description: Curating reusable design patterns for building secure and privacy-respecting agentic AI systems, documented in a problem/context/solution format.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
This workstream curates reusable design patterns intended for building secure and privacy-respecting agentic AI systems. Each pattern is documented using a format that includes problem, context, solution, and trade-offs, and is paired with relevant anti-patterns where applicable [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].

# Architecture / Specification
Topic areas covered by the catalog include:
*   Hooks and checkpointing.
*   Human-in-the-loop patterns.
*   Privacy-preserving execution (e.g., ZK proofs, TEEs, encrypted vector DBs).
*   Blast radius containment.
*   Secure memory and memory lifecycle management (retention, deletion, data sovereignty).
*   Agent containment and runtime intervention (e.g., kill switches, rollback, permission downgrade, off-task detection).
*   Agent authorization models.

# Leads
The workstream is led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4].

mutations.rationale: This workstream defines the scope and purpose of the Security and Privacy WG's effort to produce a high-level guide for builders of agentic AI systems.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
This guide provides practical, higher-level guidance for builders of agentic AI systems. It focuses on *what* builders should do, contrasting with the Design Patterns Catalog which focuses on *how* to implement specific solutions. The guide includes pointers toward recommended external frameworks and resources [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

# Architecture / Specification
Topic areas covered by the guide include:
*   Secrets management.
*   Secure tool invocation.
*   Guardrails.
*   Evaluation frameworks.
*   Post-incident forensics.
*   A curated reference section to external frameworks and resources.

# Leads
The workstream is led by Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) and Matthew Khouzam (Ericsson) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
This workstream defines a lightweight checklist and process to enable the Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) to review deliverables produced by other AAIF working groups through a security and privacy lens [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. This mechanism operationalizes the SP WG's role as an intersecting layer across the foundation.

# Architecture / Specification
Initial review targets include:
*   **Identity & Trust:** Focusing on agent identity and delegated authorization.
*   **Observability & Tracing:** Focusing on behavioral anomaly detection and audit logging.
*   **Agentic Commerce:** Focusing on payments security guardrails, fund draining prevention, account leaks, and payment-agent scope limits.
*   All other AAIF WGs as their deliverables emerge.

# Leads
The workstream is led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes open threat models, security taxonomies, control frameworks, and privacy-respecting design patterns for autonomous agents across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The group manages four primary workstreams alongside cross-working-group taxonomy collaboration, maintaining GitHub as its authoritative system of record[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its activities into specialized workstreams and cross-WG initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Conducts gap analysis of existing AI threat frameworks (OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) against agentic risks; co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. See [Threat Modeling](./sp-threat-modeling.md).
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates reusable secure and privacy-respecting agent design patterns; co-led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. See [Design Patterns](./sp-design-patterns.md).
- **Best Practices Guide**: Provides higher-level implementation guidance and external references for agent builders; co-led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. See [Best Practices](./sp-best-practices.md).
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Develops lightweight security and privacy review checklists for deliverables from other AAIF working groups; led by Govindaraj Palanisamy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. See [Review Checklist](./sp-review-checklist.md).
- **Taxonomy and Landscape**: Originally incubated within the SP WG, taxonomy work was transitioned to a cross-WG effort led by Junjie Bu, with Jay White and Katherine Druckman serving as SP WG delegates[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. See [Taxonomy and Landscape](./taxonomy-and-landscape.md).

# Lifecycle History
On 2026-06-23, the working group confirmed workstream structures, made its GitHub repositories public, and established monthly reporting alignment with the Technical Committee[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Threat Modeling Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Evaluates existing AI threat frameworks against agentic-specific threats and develops comprehensive agent threat models.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Threat Modeling Workstream performs gap analyses on existing AI threat modeling frameworks to address agentic-specific threat vectors and establish foundational security models for the AAIF[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, it serves as the near-term deliverable feeding technical guidance and patterns across the [Security and Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream evaluates existing frameworks—including OWASP, MITRE ATLAS, CSA MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF—against agentic risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Key threat vectors analyzed include:

- Memory and context poisoning[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- Multi-agent persuasion and sabotage / rogue agents[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- Tool invocation and execution risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- Excessive agency and blast radius containment[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- Delegated authorization boundaries and supply chain integrity[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]
- Commerce and payment agent risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]

# Lifecycle History
Initial gap analysis and synthesis reports were prepared in June 2026, establishing GitHub Markdown documentation as the formal system of record for deliverable tracking[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is an AAIF-wide initiative chartered to build common terminology, harmonize definitions, and resolve conflicting vocabularies across all working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Led by Junjie Bu, the workstream operates out of `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` and syncs weekly to consolidate 10–20 core terms from each working group into a unified taxonomy[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream coordinates representation across AAIF groups:

- **Security and Privacy**: Represented by delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman; incorporates concepts such as agent archetypes categorized by capabilities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Observability and Traceability**: Collaborates on core telemetry, state, and tracing definitions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Accuracy and Reliability**: Coordinates structured JSON domain slices across boundaries, grounding, failure modes, metrics, and evaluation ecosystems[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4].

# Lifecycle History
The taxonomy effort originated within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md) before being elevated to an AAIF-wide cross-WG workstream in May 2026, naming Junjie Bu as lead and seating working group delegates in June 2026[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates agent observability standards, session-level trace models, and telemetry protocols for agentic AI systems within the AAIF[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]. The group manages specialized focus groups and aligns core terminology with the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](./taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical investigations into several active focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:

- **LLM Primitives**: Conducts landscape surveys and gap analysis of LLM primitives and protocol observability models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agent State and Context**: Researches state persistence, context management, and memory system observability across academic research and production implementations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Investigates multi-agent coordination, interaction graphs, and cross-agent execution telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Explores reasoning trace models, white-box tracing, and decision-path auditability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the working group opened its GitHub repository publicly for issue tracking and deliverable management while establishing biweekly community presentation slots and monthly Technical Committee reporting cadences[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG)
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing the standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. The group focuses on classifying broad categories of failure, defining shared terminology, and providing recommendations for addressing reliability and accuracy issues proactively and reactively [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

Key strategic objectives include establishing a shared understanding of reliability and accuracy in agentic systems, providing reference approaches for measurement and detection, documenting correction patterns, and producing design guidance [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Architecture / Specification
The ARWG scope includes defining dimensions and metrics for agent accuracy and reliability, classifying failure modes, defining reliable architecture patterns (like verification loops and grounding), and standardizing recovery and corrective actions (safe-state restoration, rollback, human intervention handoff) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

The WG specifically delegates the mechanics of trace emission to the [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](Observability WG) and does not address model internals, training, or domain-specific regulatory compliance [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

The work relies on several assumptions, including the need for standardized "hooks" for state recovery, immutable agent identity standards, versioning for reproducibility, and the availability of Trust Anchors for high-stakes task verification [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Lifecycle History
The ARWG charter was approved on 2026-05-15 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. Initial work focused on three parallel tracks: taxonomy bootstrap, Deliverable 1 (D1: architectural frame for accuracy/reliability vocabulary), and Deliverable 2 (D2: applied gap analysis grounded in enterprise personas) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. D1 aims to provide a theoretical vocabulary frame, while D2 provides applied evidence and addresses concerns about scope and grounding by focusing on B2B enterprise requirements [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS) is a cross-working-group initiative responsible for developing unified terminology, definitions, and the overall landscape taxonomy for the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]. Its primary goal is to organize and harmonize terms collected from various AAIF working groups to ensure consistency and clarity across the ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Architecture / Specification
The WS employs a collaborative review process involving delegates from participating working groups. This process includes collecting terms, identifying universal terms that span multiple WGs, and reviewing them asynchronously using a unified spreadsheet [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c]. Key discussions include setting clear boundaries around the concept of an "agent" [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Lifecycle History
In June 2026, the workstream formally aligned on working group delegates and began organizing a list of universal terms. A decision was made to create a unified spreadsheet of all taxonomy terms from the various working groups to facilitate asynchronous review and feedback [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
