proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working-group AAIF initiative developing unified terminology, SKOS Lite taxonomy definitions, and CNCF-style ecosystem landscape mapping.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with creating a shared taxonomy standard and an interactive ecosystem landscape directory [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]. Its primary objective is to eliminate terminology silos and prevent duplicate research across AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Data Models and Formats

- **Taxonomy Schema**: Structured using a SKOS Lite metadata schema defining concise summaries alongside comprehensive scope notes [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Landscape Mapping**: Adopts the CNCF landscape tool format to organize member-driven and external agentic AI projects, tools, and platforms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **Decoupled Architecture**: Data repositories and web portal pipelines remain decoupled to facilitate a pull-request-driven asynchronous contribution model [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].

## Contribution and Review Process

- **Asynchronous PR Workflow**: All term proposals and updates are processed via Git pull requests [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Working Group Representation**: Each participating working group nominates one to two delegates and domain editors to review, harmonize, and attest cross-cutting terminology [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Standards Alignment**: Terminology aims for compatibility with established international standards (such as ISO and NIST), documenting explicit rationales for any necessary agentic-specific deviations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **Editorial Guidelines**: Definitions must comply with an internal style guide and an AI usage policy requiring human editorial oversight [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].

## Technical Committee Reporting

The workstream maintains a standardized monthly reporting cadence submitted to the Technical Committee (TC) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]:
- Reports are submitted by the last business day of the month as pull requests following the title format `[Report] WS-Taxonomy & Landscape – Month YYYY`.
- The TC operates a 7-calendar-day asynchronous review window prior to merging.
- Reports capture monthly summaries, progress against objectives, blockers, and explicit decisions requested from the TC [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-440eb159591a-f0f43add].

# Lifecycle History

- **May 2026**: Workstream initiated; charter reviewed and consensus reached on SKOS Lite and CNCF schema baselines [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0].
- **June 2026**: Enforced PR-driven workflow by converting legacy terms to formal PRs; secured charter approvals from six working groups; established standards harmonization policies [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].

# References

- [AAIF Landscape](../landscape/aaif-landscape.md)
- [Landscape Inclusion Criteria](../guidelines/landscape-inclusion-criteria.md)
- [Working Group Reporting Guidelines](../governance/working-group-reporting.md)
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

Chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates terminology intake and alignment across formal working group delegates[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream maintains core data schemas and publishing infrastructure:

- **Landscape Architecture**: Uses CNCF-style configuration schemas to map ecosystem runtimes, tools, and platforms in the interactive landscape portal[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].
- **Review Pipeline**: Aggregates terminology submissions from delegates into a unified spreadsheet for global conflict resolution before merging pull requests into the schema[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working-group AAIF initiative developing unified terminology, SKOS Lite taxonomy definitions, and integrating with the existing landscape project using a PR-driven workflow.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group effort dedicated to establishing unified terminology and definitions for the Agentic AI Foundation. The mission is to build a shared taxonomy, initially targeting a v1.0 release based on contributions from all working groups, using CNCF-style schemas and a PR-driven workflow [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]. The workstream also aims to integrate its ecosystem directory with the existing AAIF landscape project [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream utilizes a unified terminology spreadsheet built from contributions across all working groups, containing approximately 250 terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. The workflow involves each working group submitting 10-20 key terminologies for review [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

The review process includes:
1. Adding a consensus-based "cull" column to organize terms flagged for removal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
2. Surfacing contentious terms (such as "identity") in the shared Discord channel for broader feedback before culling or redefining them [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
3. Debating definitions, such as the distinction between "bot" and "agent" (where agents rely on AI and can hallucinate) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History
The workstream established a weekly Monday sync starting in June 2026, later agreeing to extend meetings to one hour to allow proper discussion of terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]. The initial phase involved establishing a core team of delegates from each working group and mapping out an asynchronous workflow using the shared spreadsheet [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (SPWG) establishes open threat models, security taxonomies, control frameworks, and privacy standards for agentic AI systems. The group advocates for overt alignment with external organizations such as OWASP and AARM to strengthen leverage when requesting adoption of changes (like hooks) from major AI providers (e.g., Anthropic, OpenAI) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Architecture / Specification
The SPWG manages several key workstreams:
*   **Threat Modeling:** Completed an initial gap review across eight identified areas, drawing on MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
*   **Best Practices Guide:** The first draft has been delivered for review [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
*   **Design Patterns Catalog:** A draft format has been created, though the workstream is seeking additional contributors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
*   **Review Checklist:** Developing a cross-working-group review checklist [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

The group actively participates in the cross-WG ../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md effort, reviewing the unified working sheet and contributing to the definition of terms like "bot" versus "agent" [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# Lifecycle History
The group submits monthly reports asynchronously via Pull Request format to the foundation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. The group is investigating potential overlap and collaboration opportunities with the Linux Foundation's FINOS AI governance framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

proposed_concept.title: Working Group Reporting
proposed_concept.description: Standardized monthly reporting cadence, pull request workflow, and template structure for AAIF working groups.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Working Groups (WGs) submit a monthly report to the Technical Committee (TC) to summarize progress, highlight ecosystem activity, identify blockers, and request decisions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

Reports are due by the last business day of the month. The TC review window closes 7 calendar days after submission, and the report is merged once signed off or the window closes, whichever is sooner [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

# Specification

## Workflow

1. Copy `TEMPLATE.md` into a new file named `YYYY-MM-report.md`.
2. Fill in header fields: Reporting period, Date submitted, Working Group, and Chair(s).
3. Open a pull request titled `[Report] WG <Name> – Month YYYY` and add the TC (or designated TC GitHub team) as reviewers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].
4. Update the WG's `README.md` to index the new report [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

## Required Sections

Reports must be concise, scannable, and based on recorded evidence (meeting notes, charter, git history). Sections must be included even if they contain no content, in which case "None." or "None this month." should be written [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

The required sections are [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5]:

1. **Summary:** 2–3 sentences capturing the month at a glance.
2. **Progress Against Objectives:** What shipped or advanced, tied back to stated objectives.
3. **Ecosystem Highlights:** Relevant activity, publications, or decisions happening in external groups (e.g., OWASP, AARM, MCP ACS).
4. **Blockers and Risks:** Anything the TC should be aware of.
5. **Decisions Needed from the TC:** Explicit asks stated clearly.
6. **Next Month's Focus:** Top 2–3 priorities for the coming month.
7. **Metrics / Links:** Status against charter Success Metrics (KPIs: Adoption, Quality, Community, Timeliness) and supporting links (PRs, issues, meeting notes) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-working-group AAIF initiative developing unified terminology, SKOS Lite taxonomy definitions, and maintaining the interactive ecosystem landscape map.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream (WS) curates and maintains a glossary of agentic AI terms (the Taxonomy) and an ecosystem map (the Landscape) for the AAIF [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. This ensures all Working Groups (WGs) operate from shared definitions and a unified view of the ecosystem, supporting the foundation's core pillars of Interoperability, Ecosystem Transparency, and Engineering Excellence [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

The WS is co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

# Architecture / Specification

The WS employs a model of **Federated Governance**, where curation is driven by nominated delegates (Domain Editors) representing each WG. This ensures shared definitions and landscape modifications occur through consensus [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

## Taxonomy

The WS is responsible for consolidating and standardizing core vocabulary terms using a flexible SKOS-Lite metadata schema (`prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, `contrastsWith`) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. The WS serves as the technical gatekeeper for resolving cross-cutting terminology intersections.

## Landscape

The WS maintains a living, interactive CNCF-style landscape (`landscape.yml`) whose categorization buckets evolve through delegate consensus [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

## Deliverables

Key goals include consolidating baseline terminology into a unified SKOS-Lite data repository (`taxonomy-data.js`) and deploying the fully interactive Shared Taxonomy Explorer and CNCF Landscape 2 instances to GitHub Pages [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]. The WS maintains the CI/CD pipelines for automated web dashboard publishing [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea].

# Scope Guardrails

The WS focuses on **Horizontal Curation** (consolidating cross-cutting concepts and maintaining the foundation-wide ecosystem map). Specialized domain whitepapers, low-level technical helper definitions, and execution protocol designs remain the purview of their respective vertical Technical Working Groups (**Vertical Ownership**) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group (WG) is responsible for establishing open threat models, security taxonomies, control frameworks, and privacy standards for agentic AI systems [^working-groups/security-and-privacy]. The WG is co-chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].

# Architecture / Specification

The WG operates through five established workstreams, each with confirmed leads and documented scope [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

Key deliverables currently in progress include:
*   **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis:** A first draft was presented and endorsed by the group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].
*   **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Initial content has been drafted [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

## Delegation of Taxonomy

The WG's internal effort on taxonomy has been merged into the cross-WG AAIF Taxonomy/Landscape initiative (see: ../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md). Jay White and Katherine Druckman represent the Security and Privacy WG as delegates to that initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

# Lifecycle History

In June 2026, the WG transitioned from formation into the execution phase, focusing on advancing deliverables within its five workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]. The WG noted that general availability of members and leads poses a standing risk to pacing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

The WG requested guidance from the Technical Committee regarding the scope and posture of collaboration with external groups such as OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

The goal of defining this policy is to ensure consistency in messaging, maximize influence, and consolidate efforts across the agentic AI ecosystem.

The Technical Committee (TC) is responsible for providing guidance on the scope and posture of these engagements, particularly when WGs request clarification on how to proceed with external collaboration opportunities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d].

Working Group monthly reports include a section for **Ecosystem Highlights** to track relevant activity, publications, or decisions happening in external groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group standardizing shared workflow models, execution semantics, state persistence, and external system coordination for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group ([W&PI]) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. It produces interoperability guidelines, execution semantics, and design patterns that enable agent workflows to operate across diverse frameworks, tools, and execution environments.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group addresses three foundational scope areas[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:
- **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics**: Establishing common terminology and primitives (tasks, tool calls, branching, sub-agents, retries), standard workflow representations, step execution ordering, parallelism, conditional execution paths, and agent handoff semantics.
- **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution**: Defining patterns for multi-step workflows running over extended durations, state persistence models, partial completion resumption, retries, idempotency, and workflow-level audit logs / systems of record (distinct from runtime telemetry handled by the [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) Working Group).
- **Tool Invocation and External System Coordination**: Standardizing workflow patterns for agent interactions with external systems, APIs, CLIs, and background services.

# Governance and Leadership
- **Chairs**: Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
- **Approval Date**: Approved on 2026-05-13 and updated on 2026-07-23[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group addressing agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, verifiable action records, and cross-organizational trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Identity & Trust Working Group defines standards, reference architectures, and taxonomies for autonomous agent identity, principal delegation, verifiable authorization, and cross-boundary trust frameworks within the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] Chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE), the working group coordinates core trust primitives across industry platforms, identity providers, and complementary technical initiatives.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical activities across three active sub-working groups:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

- **Taxonomy Sub-WG**: Formulating formal definitions for foundational concepts, including *Agent*, *Consent Receipt*, *Human-in-the-Loop*, and *Action Record*. The *Action Record* is conceptualized as a tamper-evident, content-private, and independently verifiable record of a consequential agent action—distinct from operator observability traces and authorization tokens.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Reference Architecture Sub-WG**: Developing a component matrix spanning Discovery Metadata, Identifiers, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758] Architectural constraints enforce that sub-agents cannot hold permissions exceeding their delegating agent or initiating user.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]
- **Critical Use Cases Sub-WG**: Defining lifecycle scenarios across Internal, B2B, and B2C interactions encompassing naming, deployment, dynamic per-request authorization, selective disclosure, and principal-attested revocation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

Additionally, the working group profiles OAuth 2.0 as the normative cross-platform authorization baseline while treating backend enforcement mechanisms as application-autonomous, and integrates industry models such as NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace (SAW) and the OpenID Foundation's identity management specifications.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]

# References

- [Identity Management for Agentic AI (OpenID Foundation)](https://openid.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Identity-Management-for-Agentic-AI.pdf)
- [NVIDIA Secure Agent Workspace Reference Design](https://docs.nvidia.com/enterprise-reference-architectures/secure-agent-workspace-reference-design/latest/what-is-secure-agent-workspace.html)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications and reference architectures for autonomous agent commerce workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group develops protocol-neutral capability maps, comparative protocol analyses, and reference architectures for agent-driven commerce transactions.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760] Chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI), the group establishes shared abstractions across the full transactional lifecycle, including product discovery, stateful checkout negotiation, payment execution, fraud mitigation, and post-purchase dispute handling.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]

# Architecture / Specification

The group's primary deliverable is the **Agentic Commerce Capability Map**, which benchmarks protocols such as the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP), Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), and Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) against key transactional interfaces:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760][^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]

- **Discovery**: Separating static asynchronous product catalog feeds from dynamic live merchant queries, addressing source discovery, catalog normalization, freshness, and trust.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **Checkout & Negotiation**: Evaluating merchant-authoritative negotiation flows, extensible transport bindings, and human-in-the-loop handoffs across ACP and UCP.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760]
- **Payment Handlers**: Decomposing payment execution into three reusable abstractions—*handler*, *instrument*, and *credential*—and analyzing delegated tokenization, dynamic eligibility, and challenge-credential-receipt patterns from MPP.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393]
- **Fraud & Trust Signals**: Distinguishing agent identity and risk profiles from shopper identity and risk profiles, while preserving portable attestations and intent-binding evidence across merchant, payment provider, and platform boundaries without indiscriminate data disclosure.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]

The working group coordinates inter-group dependencies with [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Security & Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), and [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe]

# References

- [WG Agentic Commerce Charter](https://github.com/aaif/wg-agentic-commerce/blob/main/charter.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications and reference architectures for agent-driven commerce.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (WG) is focused on standardizing the protocols, specifications, and reference architectures necessary for agents to participate effectively in commercial transactions. The WG aims to address the broad set of concerns arising from agent involvement in commerce, including product discoverability, transaction execution, identity and delegated authority, fraud and liability, human oversight, merchant integration burden, and disputes [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].

The group identified several existing efforts as inputs, including UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol), ACP (Agent Communication Protocol), AP2 (Authorization Protocol 2), and x402 (Payment Request Protocol) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].

# Architecture / Specification
The WG is developing a **Capability Map**, **Gap Analysis**, and **Reference Architecture** for agentic commerce [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

Initial analysis showed that agents require capabilities beyond simple order visibility and payment execution. They need policy, consent, delegated-authority, negotiation, and mutation capabilities related to the transaction lifecycle, especially for post-purchase workflows like cancellation, return, or refund [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

The group mapped agent wallets and x402-style payment responses as contributors of payment or credential capabilities, noting that protocols like AP2 illustrate how bounded intent might accompany payment [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

proposed_concept.description: A structured process and tool used by the AAIF Observability and Traceability WG to generate reference architecture assessments for AI/agent technologies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Reference Architecture Skill (`aaif-ref-arch`) is a defined process and associated tool used primarily by the Observability and Traceability Working Group to produce structured reference architecture documents and evaluation assessments for AI agent technologies, frameworks, and specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

The skill is designed to analyze open-source AI agent tools, frameworks, or specifications and provide a standardized assessment of their architecture, instrumentation, and telemetry capabilities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

# Architecture / Specification
The process involves four main steps:
1. **Gather Source Material:** Fetching documentation, architecture docs, and schema definitions to identify core components, data models, APIs, and runtime behavior.
2. **Produce Reference Architecture Document:** Generating a structured Markdown file detailing the technology.
3. **Produce Evaluation Assessment:** (Details truncated in source, but listed as a step).
4. **Commit:** Committing the resulting documents.

The Reference Architecture Document structure requires specific sections, including:
*   **Objective** and **Scope / Zoom Level** (e.g., primitive layer, orchestration layer, or system layer).
*   **Prerequisites** (pinned versions of components).
*   **Architecture Diagram** (ASCII diagram showing components, data flows, and telemetry emission points).
*   **Instrumentation Walkthrough** (what is captured and the mechanism used).
*   **Sample Trace Output**.
*   **Cost Profile**.
*   **Validation Criteria**.
*   **Limitations / Out of Scope** [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

The skill requires internet access and git CLI, and is compatible with runtimes such as `kiro` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern requiring an identified human principal to explicitly authorize an immutable proposal before execution of a protected effect.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The human approval gate pattern addresses workflow scenarios where an agent reaches an action whose risk, audit obligations, or ownership requires judgment from an accountable human before execution occurs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]. The pattern ensures that the approval decision binds directly and immutably to the exact proposal presented, keeping the workflow safely parked in a durable state until an explicit decision is recorded [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

Developed under the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), it is used within composed architectures such as single-agent processes with human approval and operates alongside companion patterns including the proposal/execution split and durable wait [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-20].

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern relies on four core capability roles: an execution engine, a human interaction surface, a state/context store, and an audit log [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

### Invariants
Implementations must guarantee the following invariants regardless of the underlying runtime platform [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]:
- **Identified Approver:** The approver must be a uniquely identified human principal authorized for the decision category; shared approval credentials are not permitted [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Immutable Proposal Presentation:** The presentation surface must display the exact, immutable proposal version to which the decision binds [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Explicit Decision:** Approval and rejection must be explicit actions. Timeouts, silence, delivery failures, or system errors never imply approval [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Audit Traceability:** The decision record captures the proposal version, approver identity, decision value, and timestamp under the same run execution identity [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Supersession Invalidation:** Any modification or supersession of a proposal invalidates previous state and requires a fresh approval decision [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Bounded Waiting:** Pending approvals must define deadlines with explicit expiration or escalation pathways [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Execution Idempotency:** Duplicate, late, or conflicting decision events cannot trigger multiple run resumptions or executions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Reference Architecture Model
proposed_concept.description: Framework organizing workflow reference architectures around practitioner operational jobs and reusable patterns rather than agent topology.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The job-oriented reference architecture model is an organizing methodology proposed by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) that structures reference architectures around recognizable operational goals rather than agent counts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

The approach recognizes that agent topology (single-agent vs. multi-agent) is an implementation outcome rather than a starting requirement, allowing practitioners to navigate architectures based on required guarantees, risk boundaries, and capabilities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-20].

# Architecture / Specification
The framework establishes a clear separation between architectures and patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62]:
- **Reference Architectures:** Complete compositions of reusable patterns, required system capabilities, operational boundaries, guarantees, and exit states aligned to a distinct practitioner job [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- **Workflow Patterns:** Independently adoptable solutions to recurring sub-problems (such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), proposal/execution split, and durable wait) with their own invariants, failure modes, and implementation approaches [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-20].
- **Scope Boundaries:** Disparate authorization mechanisms (e.g., human approval vs. policy-driven authorization) are structured as separate architectures due to differences in attribution topology and risk profile [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-20].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group standardizing telemetry models, trace context propagation, and cross-agent execution observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry models, trace context propagation, and execution observability across heterogeneous AI agent frameworks and runtimes. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group develops reference specifications, gap analyses, and telemetry schemas for observing agent behaviors, resource discovery, and peer-to-peer interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical work into three active focus tracks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability**: Led by Zayne Turner, focusing on Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) observability (skill discovery, provenance, and pre-execution trust tracing), skill lifecycle observability, and cross-boundary telemetry gap models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination)**: Led by Ty Smith, focusing on multi-agent execution graphs, context intelligence runtime telemetry, and coordination tracing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Agentic State & Context**: Led by Govindaraj, covering reasoning traces, memory and state observability, and landscape gap analysis[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

Key collaborative specifications and work items include:
- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: Application-layer telemetry proposal formulating recommendations for the OpenTelemetry (OTEL) core specification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Verifiable Telemetry & Peer-to-Peer Observability**: Joint exploration with LibP2P evaluating Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO), Agent Action Capsules (AAC), and CBOR-encoded telemetry for composable trust across decentralized agent networks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-07**: Consolidated focus group structure from five groups to three active tracks to optimize contributor bandwidth and eliminate overlapping scopes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **2026-08**: Initiated technical collaboration on peer-to-peer telemetry standards and Verifiable Telemetry Objects with LibP2P contributors[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Design Specification
proposed_concept.description: A formal, machine-readable specification and design methodology for defining agentic workflows across deterministic and autonomous execution modes.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflow Design Specification (WDS) is a proposed formal, machine-readable artifact for defining agentic workflows, developed in the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21]. It pairs with a Workflow Design Method (WDM) to transform business use cases into standardized blueprints that can be executed directly by coding agents or human software engineers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification framework is structured around three key design principles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-21]:
- **Unified Spectrum Coverage**: Spans deterministic, model-assisted, and agent-driven workflows within a single vocabulary, treating agent count not as an organizing principle but as an outcome of recommending the least-agentic pattern suitable for the task.
- **Shared Artifact (WDS)**: Provides a single structured specification capturing target workflow architecture, execution boundaries, state requirements, and integration points for downstream implementation.
- **Formal Design Method (WDM)**: Outlines repeatable steps to translate business requirements into a valid WDS, designed for interchangeable execution by human architects and AI agents.

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing a shared workflow model, common terminology, interoperability guidelines, and design patterns that allow agent workflows to operate across frameworks, tools, and execution environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

The working group organizes its technical outputs across several workstreams:
- **Taxonomy**: Establishes core terminology and shared vocabulary for agentic workflows to reduce ambiguity across specifications and use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Reference Architectures**: Develops architecture patterns applying workflow standards and models[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Explores and documents operational enterprise workflow use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].

The working group collaborates with other foundation groups including [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), and [Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Best Practices workstream operates under the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to develop practical, high-level implementation guidance and security control patterns for builders of agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream produces the *Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide*, structured around failure patterns, controls, and decision frameworks across five core domains[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
- **Secrets Management**: Credential hygiene, runtime scoping, and protection for agent environments.
- **Secure Tool Invocation**: Tool security, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, and supply chain integrity.
- **Guardrails**: Input and output boundary enforcement and defensive filters.
- **Evaluation Frameworks**: Red-teaming and safety benchmark methodologies.
- **Post-Incident Forensics**: Forensic readiness, audit capture, and post-compromise investigation.

Identity architectures and delegated authorization models (such as SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693) are explicitly out of scope for this deliverable and are addressed by the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) body dedicated to convening practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish a shared understanding of agent observability [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe]. The group aligns existing ecosystem efforts, identifies gaps, and produces specifications and guidance where no existing standards body addresses the need [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe].

Its technical focus sits at the intersection of agent reasoning, behavior, and execution with observable signals and trace structures, emphasizing interoperability across agent runtimes, frameworks, and tooling [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe].

# Leadership and Operations

- **Chair**: Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe]
- **Co-Chair**: Matthew Lee (Datadog) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe]
- **Term**: March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe]
- **Meetings**: Biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe]
- **Reporting Cadence**: Monthly reports submitted to the Technical Committee [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-c75477fe] following standard reporting guidelines (see [../governance/working-group-reporting.md](../governance/working-group-reporting.md)).

# Working Methods

The working group utilizes an issue-driven GitHub operating model as its single durable source of truth [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-13]:

- **Work Tracking**: Every deliverable, focus group task, cross-working-group coordination thread, or decision is tracked via standard GitHub issue templates [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b44b5d93b435-bb190e50].
- **Status Lifecycle**: Work items use standardized status states (`needs owner`, `scoping`, `in progress`, `ready for review`, `blocked`, `done`) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff].
- **Artifact Flow**: Early drafting may occur in shared documents, but durable deliverables and reference materials transition to repository pull requests for formal review and merging [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b2496e80299b-e136231b].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing open threat models, security control frameworks, design patterns, and cross-working-group security review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. The working group develops open threat models, best practice guidance, reusable design patterns, and cross-working-group review checklists to enable providers and consumers to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

# Governance and Operations

- **Chairs**: Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google), serving appointed terms from March 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- **Cadence**: Biweekly meetings on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].
- **Transparency**: Past meeting recordings, notes, GitHub repositories, and Discord channels operate under a default-to-open posture [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Deliverable Approval Process**: Deliverables within the approved charter scope may be reviewed and merged directly by the working group without awaiting formal [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) approval, with the TC tracking merged deliverables through [monthly reports](../governance/working-group-reporting.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The working group executes its mission across four primary workstreams alongside cross-WG initiatives:

1. [Threat Modeling](./sp-threat-modeling.md): Comprehensive agentic AI threat modeling framework and gap analysis against existing AI security standards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
2. [Best Practices](./sp-best-practices.md): Practical security and privacy implementation guides for agent developers and deployers [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
3. [Design Patterns](./sp-design-patterns.md): Catalog of vetted architectural design patterns for secure agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
4. [Cross-WG Review Checklist](./sp-review-checklist.md): Standardized review process and checklist for evaluating security and privacy across all AAIF working group deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
5. [Taxonomy and Landscape](./taxonomy-and-landscape.md): Joint cross-WG terminology definitions covering security, guardrails, and constraints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

proposed_concept.title: Security & Privacy: Threat Modeling Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Evaluates existing AI threat frameworks against agentic-specific threats and develops comprehensive threat modeling frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Threat Modeling workstream of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md) develops an open threat modeling framework tailored specifically to agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. The effort evaluates existing AI and classical cybersecurity frameworks to identify gaps in addressing autonomous agent architectures, multi-agent coordination, and tool execution risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

- **Lead Contributors**: Fernando Lucktemberg and Alon Mazor [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Evaluated Baseline Frameworks**: Gap analysis assesses coverage against MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) across eight defined security areas [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Methodology Evaluation**: The workstream is actively evaluating alignment between agentic threat models and classical methodologies including STRIDE and PASTA [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Scope Integrations**: Deliverable revisions incorporate UI/Human-User Accountability (HUA) considerations, supply-chain vulnerabilities, and emerging protocol security developments such as Model Context Protocol (MCP) stateless operation and tool attestation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Initial gap analysis across the eight target areas drafted and submitted as a pull request to the working group repository [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- **August 2026**: Review cycle opened for community feedback and integration of STRIDE/PASTA mappings and UI/HUA considerations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Overview

The Best Practices workstream within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md) creates operational and development guidelines for securing agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed]. The guide provides actionable control recommendations for agent runtimes, tool invocation, human oversight, and data privacy safeguards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

- **Lead Contributors**: Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Deliverable Scope**: Covers foundational security controls, operational deployment hardening, and human-in-the-loop oversight mechanisms [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Cross-WG Boundary**: The workstream coordinates with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](./identity-and-trust.md) so that agent identity, attestation, and authorization sections are aligned with and owned by the Identity group [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Accountability Model**: Aligns with the foundational posture that agents perform actions while humans retain ultimate accountability and responsibility [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Workstream held its inaugural meeting and published the first skeleton draft as a pull request on GitHub [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-10].
- **August 2026**: Workstream began integrating review feedback, establishing cross-WG identity alignment, and incorporating human-user accountability (HUA) guidelines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.description: Curates reusable design patterns for building secure and privacy-respecting agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Design Patterns Catalog workstream of the [Security and Privacy Working Group](./security-and-privacy.md) curates standardized, reusable architectural patterns that mitigate security vulnerabilities and enforce privacy guarantees in agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Architecture / Specification

- **Lead Contributors**: Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Deliverable Artifacts**: A structured catalog charter, pattern authoring template, and standardized pattern entries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Scope Alignment**: The workstream coordinates with reference architecture initiatives to clearly divide pattern coverage between foundational security/privacy design patterns (such as [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)) and operational workflow architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Completed catalog structure and charter definition in drafting documents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **August 2026**: Shared initial pattern template for contributor submissions and prepared the draft for pull request submission to the AAIF GitHub repository [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Overview

The Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist workstream defines a lightweight review framework and verification checklist to help peer AAIF working groups identify and address security and privacy risks in their specifications and architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Architecture / Specification

- **Lead Contributor**: Govindaraj Palanisamy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **Objectives**: Establish cross-functional review criteria covering threat analysis, identity delegation, data isolation, and auditable telemetry across all Foundation outputs without blocking workstream velocity [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Inter-Group Coordination**: Conducts a cross-document gap analysis with other AAIF working groups to prevent overlapping mandates and align security review touchpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Lifecycle History

- **July 2026**: Workstream lead initiated information gathering across AAIF working groups and established administrative structure [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed].
- **August 2026**: Convened first workstream meeting with working group leads and commenced cross-WG deliverable gap analysis [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

proposed_concept.title: Project Lifecycle Policy
proposed_concept.description: Intake process, review criteria, stage progression (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual review rules for open source projects in the AAIF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Project Lifecycle Policy establishes the governance rules and formal processes for open technical projects joining, progressing through, and retiring within the foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Administered by the Technical Committee (TC) under the terms of the AAIF Charter, the policy provides a predictable path for projects across four distinct lifecycle stages: Sandbox, Growth, Impact, and Emeritus [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

Progression across lifecycle stages allows projects to participate at maturity levels matched to their governance, community adoption, and technical validation, ensuring access to AAIF mentorship and foundation resources [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Process

Projects must apply via the `aaif/project-proposals` repository by submitting a comprehensive intake application [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Key proposal requirements include:
- Project description, origin, use cases, and alignment with the AAIF mission.
- OSI-approved permissive license and public repository location.
- Documented governance model (`GOVERNANCE.md`), core maintainer lists, and public communication channels.
- Release mechanics, automated CI/CD validation, public issue trackers, and external dependency licensing.
- Optional details regarding a Technical Committee sponsor and cross-project integrations.

## Lifecycle Stages

1. **Sandbox Stage**: Entry-level stage for early-stage or experimental projects meeting basic requirements (OSI license, public repo, mission alignment) [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
2. **Growth Stage**: Intermediate stage for projects demonstrating active adoption, defined release processes, open governance, and an expanding contributor base [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
3. **Impact Stage**: Mature, flagship projects exhibiting high production adoption, robust multi-organizational governance, comprehensive security practices, and proven ecosystem impact [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].
4. **Emeritus Stage**: End-of-life status for inactive or deprecated projects transitioning away from active development while preserving historical project assets [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

## Annual Review Process

The Technical Committee evaluates all active projects annually to assess continued alignment, health metrics, governance vitality, and stage graduation readiness [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# References

- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- [Working Group Submission Guidelines](../governance/wg-submission-guidelines.md)

mutations.rationale: Creates a draft security design pattern defining hardware-isolated policy enforcement and remote attestation boundaries for agent execution.

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Security design pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing inside a hardware TEE while keeping dynamic agent execution outside the trust boundary.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Attested Isolated Runtime is a security design pattern for agentic deployments where infrastructure operators sit within the threat model [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. The pattern separates policy enforcement and cryptographic evidence generation from dynamic agent execution by placing the Policy Decision Point (PDP) and evidence signer inside a hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), while keeping agent runtime code outside the trusted computing base [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

By ensuring that data release and tool execution are gated on independent verifier appraisal of cryptographic measurements, the pattern restricts unauthorized infrastructure manipulation without expanding the trusted boundary to untrusted agent inputs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Requirements

The pattern defines four structural elements [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:
1. **External Agent Placement**: The agent engine remains outside the hardware-isolated boundary because agent code executes attacker-influenced inputs, avoiding unnecessary expansion of the trusted computing base.
2. **Internal Key Generation**: The evidence-signing key is generated strictly inside the isolated boundary and bound directly to runtime measurements.
3. **Policy Sealing**: Policy bundles, tool schemas, model weight digests, and system prompts are sealed to the hardware measurement and unlocked only upon verified appraisal.
4. **Independent Verifier Appraisal**: Evidence per unit of work is appraised by an independent relying-party verifier (aligned with RFC 9334 RATS architecture).

## Implementation Spectrum and Limits

- **Hardware & Standards Neutrality**: Designed to work across AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, ARM CCA, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing, and TPM 2.0 architectures, alongside RFC 9334, RFC 9711, RFC 8747, and IETF SCITT standards [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Software-Only Emulation**: Supports software-only execution modes for local development, continuous integration, and non-confidential environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Explicit Limitations**: The pattern does not prevent prompt injection, algorithmic bias, or side-channel leakage; it isolates enforcement and verification mechanics from operator compromise [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# References

- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- [SP Design Patterns Workstream](../working-groups/sp-design-patterns.md)
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group standardizing telemetry models, trace context propagation, cross-agent execution observability, and cross-surface identity resolution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group standardizes telemetry models, trace context propagation, span semantics, and execution observability for agentic AI workflows across disparate platforms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-27]. The working group establishes uniform mechanisms to monitor multi-agent interactions, trace step-by-step decision loops, attribute resource costs, and guarantee end-to-end auditability.

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Deliverables and Use Case Taxonomy

The working group organizes telemetry and operational requirements into structured categories:
- **Cost and Outcomes (Category B)**: Tracking aggregate cost, token consumption, and cost per task outcome across execution harnesses.
- **Code and Artifact Attribution (Category C)**: Correlating agent interventions with downstream code and repository state changes.
- **Compliance and Auditability (Category E)**: Verifiable audit trails capturing decision sequences, input contexts, and safety evaluations.
- **Identity and Ownership (Category I)**: Standardizing cross-surface identity resolution (Use Case I1) to map fragmented actor interactions (IDE, CLI, CI, and cloud API sessions) back to a canonical human or organizational principal responsible for operational cost and risk [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-27].

# References

- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)
- [AAIF Reference Architecture Skill](../methodology/aaif-reference-architecture-skill.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: An AAIF repository and tooling framework providing automated, prompt-injection-resilient issue analysis and triage skills for maintainers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an Agentic AI Foundation repository and utility providing automated triage and structured technical analysis for incoming issues and pull request submissions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. Designed for repository maintainers, it executes agentic evaluation workflows using standardized templates and historical reference analyses while enforcing defensive prompt-injection guardrails [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].

# Architecture / Specification
The repository implements modular agent skills—such as the `issue-analysis` skill (see `../methodology/issue-analysis-skill.md`)—along with injection test fixtures and evaluation templates [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60]:

- **Prompt Injection Defense**: Untrusted issue bodies are isolated within nonce-delimited data blocks. Directive injection attempts (e.g., mass notifications, command execution requests) are captured as diagnostic findings via `injectionSuspected` and `injectionNotes` rather than executed [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-04ecd65ab81f-33714e60].
- **Read-Only Codebase Grounding**: Triage agents inspect local repository source files to identify affected modules without modifying code or invoking arbitrary network and build commands [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
- **Historical Precedent Grounding**: Analyses reference curated past reviews to calibrate severity classifications, reproducibility assessments, and suggested remediation steps against maintainer conventions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: A structured agent skill methodology for classifying GitHub issues, forming root-cause hypotheses, and proposing maintainer actions while mitigating prompt injection.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis Skill is an agentic workflow specification defined in the AAIF `submission-analyser` repository (see `../project/submission-analyser.md`) to produce structured first-pass technical assessments of filed GitHub issues [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]. It establishes a four-step triage procedure that classifies issues, evaluates severity against historical precedents, inspects the codebase in read-only mode, and treats untrusted issue inputs safely [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill defines four primary operational phases [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]:

1. **Evidence Isolation and Adversarial Input Detection**: Issue content is ingested strictly as data within nonce delimiters. Meta-instructions or injection attempts are noted in `injectionSuspected` and `injectionNotes` while the underlying technical facts are evaluated [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
2. **Codebase Inspection**: The agent inspects checked-out repository files to identify concrete paths (`src/...`) and verify the plausibility of reported behavior under a read-only policy [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690].
3. **Historical Precedent Grounding**: The agent reviews existing maintainer analyses in `references/` to match tags and components, adopting established criteria for severity rating and root-cause determination [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4754a1b8e47b-9ed9890b].
4. **Structured Report Formulation**: Output is formatted according to a standardized schema covering Summary, Classification (`Type`, `Severity`, `Reproducibility`), Affected Components, Root-cause Hypotheses, Suggested Actions, Open Questions, and Related Past Reviews [^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef][^evt-submission-analyser-file-20fc496a9225-9e278b3d][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6d47851ad176-ba0f0f22].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: AAIF repository and tooling framework providing automated, prompt-injection-resilient issue analysis and triage.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
`submission-analyser` is an AAIF repository and tooling framework that automates issue triage and classification while maintaining resilience against adversarial prompt injection attacks. It implements structured validation rules aligned with [Issue Analysis Skill](../methodology/issue-analysis-skill.md) to inspect incoming submissions safely.

# Architecture / Specification
The project includes an adversarial test suite in `tests/fixtures/injections/` designed to validate analyzer robustness across multiple injection modalities:
- **Direct Instruction Overrides**: Payloads attempting to clear system instructions, extract system prompts, or force arbitrary responses [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Hidden Comments**: Payloads concealed within HTML comments to manipulate analysis parameters such as severity and injection detection flags [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe].
- **Untrusted Link Payloads**: Submissions instructing the agent to fetch remote payloads, execute diffs, or exfiltrate analysis [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].
- **Synthetic Tool Invocations**: Payloads embedding fabricated tool execution or function call syntax (`<function_calls>`, `tool_call`) to trigger unauthorized actions [^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].
- **Encoding & Obfuscation**: Directives obfuscated via Base64, ROT13, or Cyrillic homoglyphs designed to evade naive keyword matching [^evt-submission-analyser-file-0f27825af60d-1d3aca33].
- **Role-Play & Invisible Characters**: Attacks utilizing zero-width characters, bidirectional text overrides, and persona adoption to bypass guardrails [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].

# References
- [AAIF Submission Analyser Repository](https://github.com/aaif/submission-analyser)

mutations.rationale: Add reference architecture for PyTorch Profiler tracing from Python op dispatch to GPU kernel execution.

proposed_concept.title: PyTorch Profiler Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for capturing tensor operations and GPU kernel execution traces via PyTorch Profiler into Chrome Trace format.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The PyTorch Profiler reference architecture demonstrates how PyTorch's built-in profiling instrumentation captures the full execution path of tensor operations—from Python-level operator dispatch through the C++ ATen backend to GPU kernel execution on hardware accelerators[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]. Developed within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), this reference architecture bridges framework-level semantics (such as model layers and optimizer steps) with underlying hardware execution details (such as CUDA/HIP kernels, memory allocations, and collective communications)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7].

# Architecture / Specification

The profiler operates across Python user code, PyTorch ATen dispatcher hooks, and GPU execution backends using the bundled Kineto tracing library[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]:

- **Python User Code**: Instrumentation occurs via the `torch.profiler.profile` context manager, tracking execution iterations and marking step boundaries with `prof.step()`.
- **Dispatcher and Hooks**: ATen operator dispatch triggers `RecordFunction` callbacks that capture operator names, input tensor shapes, data types, and stack traces.
- **Hardware Tracing**: Leverages CUPTI (on NVIDIA via CUDA Toolkit 12.x+) or roctracer (on AMD via ROCm 6.x+) to record kernel launches, memory allocations/deallocations, and execution timing.
- **Output Formats**: Generates standardized Chrome Trace JSON (`traceEvents` array) exportable for analysis in Chrome tracing (`chrome://tracing`), Perfetto, TensorBoard (via `tensorboard_trace_handler`), and Holistic Trace Analysis (HTA).

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: AAIF repository and tooling framework providing automated, prompt-injection-resilient issue analysis and triage.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Submission Analyser is an automated issue analysis and triage tool designed to safely process untrusted user submissions, GitHub issues, and PR comments while resisting indirect prompt injection attacks[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].

# Architecture / Specification

The project maintains an adversarial test fixture suite covering common prompt injection vectors to validate resilience against malicious inputs[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea][^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61]:

- **Environment Variable and Secret Exfiltration**: Test cases evaluate resilience against attempts to extract sensitive runtime tokens (such as `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, or service account credentials) via structured summary fields or payload smuggling[^evt-submission-analyser-file-c385a440d3d1-196a4a61].
- **Fake Authority and Urgency Spoofing**: Test cases simulating operator, foundation security, or model safety authority claims designed to coerce the analyser into bypassing egress policies or clearing injection flags[^evt-submission-analyser-file-e761e6213598-a8166ad6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-fdb9d913d85d-8ad69d31].
- **Delimiter and Block Forging**: Evaluates handling of forged system/untrusted delimiter boundaries and XML/HTML tagging designed to prematurely escape untrusted content blocks[^evt-submission-analyser-file-f4ad28ba849d-48065e61].
- **Nested Comments and Mentions**: Tests parser handling of nested HTML comments, group mentions, and payload injection within collapsible `<details>` blocks[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].

proposed_concept.title: OpenTelemetry for AI Agent Infrastructure
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for OpenTelemetry telemetry collection, processing, and gen_ai semantic conventions across AI agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

OpenTelemetry (OTel) provides a vendor-neutral observability framework defining how traces, metrics, and logs are instrumented, collected, processed, and exported across AI agent infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]. Developed as an industry telemetry substrate and evaluated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), OTel standardizes span hierarchies and attribute definitions for LLM gateways, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

# Architecture / Specification

The OTel reference architecture spans application instrumentation, wire protocols, and collector processing pipelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]:

- **Instrumentation & Semantic Conventions**: Agent runtimes and LLM gateways use language SDKs (such as Python, Java, and Go) to emit traces adhering to standardized `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions capturing prompt configurations, token counts, model identifiers, and tool execution spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Transport (OTLP)**: OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) transports telemetry over gRPC (port 4317) or HTTP/Protobuf/JSON (port 4318) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Collector Pipeline**: The OTel Collector receives telemetry from multiple sources, processes records via batching, filtering, and attribute redaction, and exports them to backend storage and visualization platforms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

mutations.rationale: Documents the reference architecture for the Agent Trace specification tracking code attribution in AI coding agent environments.

proposed_concept.title: Agent Trace Specification
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for the Agent Trace open specification enabling line-level code attribution from AI coding agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent Trace is an open specification designed to capture line-level code attribution traces generated by AI coding agents within version-controlled repositories [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]. It provides a vendor-neutral format to record which models, sessions, and edit operations produced specific modifications across codebases [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

# Architecture / Specification

Operating as a local-first telemetry format at the primitive session layer, Agent Trace records file modifications and tool invocations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]:

- **Hook Dispatches**: Agent environments (such as Cursor and Claude Code) trigger hook events on actions like file edits, tab completions, and shell executions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **Trace Dispatcher**: Event payloads are piped via stdin JSON to a hook dispatcher script (`trace-hook.ts`) executing on the Bun runtime [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **Persistence**: Trace records are appended directly to local repository storage in `.agent-trace/traces.jsonl`, binding edits to specific file paths, contributor metadata, and revision history without requiring a remote collector [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

mutations.rationale: Documents the reference architecture for Linux FTrace kernel tracing within the observability stack.

proposed_concept.title: FTrace Kernel Function Tracing
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for Linux FTrace kernel function tracing, tracefs filesystem interface, and dynamic NOP-to-call patching.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

FTrace is the built-in Linux kernel tracing framework providing low-overhead function tracing, function graph recording, and static tracepoint capture [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]. Assessed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) as a foundational OS-level tracing mechanism, FTrace offers system-wide observability without requiring external kernel modules [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].

# Architecture / Specification

FTrace relies on kernel compiler support and per-CPU ring buffers accessed through a virtual filesystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]:

- **Dynamic Patching**: Kernel functions compiled with `-pg` or `-mfentry` insert 5-byte NOP instructions at entry points. When tracing is enabled, NOPs are dynamically patched to calls targeting `ftrace_caller` via `text_poke_bp`, achieving near-zero overhead when disabled [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].
- **Filesystem Interface**: Configuration and telemetry retrieval are controlled via `tracefs` (mounted at `/sys/kernel/tracing/`), providing human-readable text output as well as binary ring buffers consumed by tools like `trace-cmd` and KernelShark [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].
- **Tracer Capabilities**: Supports function execution tracing, call duration graphs (`function_graph`), static tracepoints, and in-kernel histogram aggregation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1].

mutations.rationale: Documents the aggregate comparative evaluation of Linux kernel tracing technologies across AAIF evaluation dimensions.

proposed_concept.title: Linux Kernel Tracing Comparison (LTTng, perf, FTrace)
proposed_concept.description: Comparative assessment of LTTng, perf, and FTrace across overhead, interfaces, and observability dimensions for system infrastructure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Linux kernel tracing comparative assessment evaluates LTTng, perf, and FTrace across foundational observability and infrastructure performance dimensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]. Conducted by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the analysis establishes the relative strengths, data path architectures, and overhead profiles of core Linux tracing frameworks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef, ^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-69d00b3de313-41c8aea6].

# Architecture / Specification

The three frameworks specialize in distinct tracing paradigms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef]:

- **LTTng**: Implements external kernel modules and userspace tracing (LTTng-UST) with lock-free per-CPU ring buffers, exporting structured binary traces in Common Trace Format (CTF) for high-throughput, low-overhead production monitoring [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **Linux perf**: Focuses on hardware Performance Monitoring Unit (PMU) counters, statistical sampling, and dynamic userspace probes (uprobes/USDT), utilizing per-event memory-mapped ring buffers and `perf.data` files [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
- **FTrace**: Built directly into the Linux kernel with zero external package dependencies, using dynamic binary NOP patching and text-based `tracefs` interfaces for function call graphing and kernel subsystem debugging [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-313867ac2247-613905ef].
