proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the 6-step workflow, engagement bar, automated intake agent, and onboarding process for AAIF project submissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Project Proposal Process is the standard operating workflow for proposing, reviewing, approving, and onboarding open-source projects into the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. While the [Project Lifecycle](../governance/project-lifecycle.md) establishes lifecycle stages (such as Sandbox, Growth, and Impact) and review criteria [^evt-technical-committee-pr-9], this process governs the operational intake pipeline.

The process enforces a distributed engagement model: rather than requiring a single dedicated sponsor, submissions must satisfy a minimum engagement bar across members of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) during an offline Q&A window before moving to a formal vote [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Execution Pipeline

The operating process consists of six sequential steps, one parallel step, and an optional on-demand presentation [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:

1. **Initial Intake (Offline)**: The CTO screens submissions for completeness and technical fit, assisted by an automated intake agent that performs public compliance checks and private advisory reviews.
2. **TC Q&A Window (Offline)**: The Technical Committee reviews the proposal asynchronously via GitHub issues. If the minimum engagement bar is not met, TC chairs appoint an on-demand TC supporter to drive review or reject the submission.
   - *Optional Presentation (Live)*: Scheduled on demand if a TC member specifically requests a live presentation.
   - *Contributor Paperwork (Parallel)*: Submitter executes necessary contribution disclosures and legal preparation via the LF PMO.
3. **TC Vote (Offline)**: The Technical Committee votes on project admission and initial lifecycle tier using LFX Vote.
4. **Governing Board Approval (Offline)**: The Governing Board votes to confirm organizational readiness, funding, and resource allocation.
5. **Legal Formation (Offline)**: Linux Foundation Legal and AAIF staff finalize the technical charter, contribution agreement, and trademark transfers via DocuSign.
6. **Technical Onboarding (Offline)**: LF IT and the submitter complete repository migration and infrastructure integration.

# Lifecycle History

- **v0.3 (August 28, 2026)**: Defined operating procedure with 6-step sequential pipeline, engagement bar mechanics, automated intake agent role, and decoupled TC supporter on-demand trigger [^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Create Online Series Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill for provisioning recurring AAIF online event series in Google Drive by cloning TemplateSeries and rebranding assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

`aaif-create-online-series` is an operational agent skill designed to provision and bootstrap new Agentic AI Foundation online event programs (such as reading groups, paper clubs, webinars, and virtual panel series) in Google Drive [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6]. It acts as the online counterpart to `aaif-create-chapter`.

Online series reside in the top-level `Online/` Drive workspace and clone the `TemplateSeries` structure, creating dedicated trackers, attendee CRMs, and design asset folders without physical venue fields [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Tooling Rules

- **Drive Interface**: Driven strictly via the `gws` CLI and Python. Native Google Workspace files (`application/vnd.google-apps.*`) are manipulated via Docs/Sheets/Slides APIs.
- **OOXML Byte Manipulation**: Direct zip/XML manipulation is reserved for stored Office files (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`). Desktop suites (e.g., LibreOffice / `soffice`, `unoconv`) are strictly prohibited to prevent font substitution and OOXML degradation [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6].
- **Slide Previews**: Rendered via `aaif_events.slides_export.render_slide_png` API instead of local conversion [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-e7b736d6].

## Rebranding Transforms

When instantiating `TemplateSeries`, the skill applies token replacement while preserving template structure:
- Replaces `San Francisco` / `SAN FRANCISCO` tokens with the target series name.
- Expands `SF` abbreviations to the full series name.
- Replaces default Luma slugs (`aaif-sanfrancisco` / `aaif-sf`) with series-specific slugs (`aaif-<slug>`).
- Incorporates standardized AAIF lockup footers into template decks [^evt-community-events-pr-31].

mutations.rationale: Define the core workflow pattern separating agentic action proposal from workflow-governed execution, referenced across multiple job-oriented reference architectures.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Workflow design pattern separating non-deterministic agent proposal generation from deterministic, workflow-controlled side-effect execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Proposal/Execution Split is a workflow architectural pattern cataloged by the [Workflows and Process Integration WG](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424]. The pattern decouples the reasoning component that generates an action proposal from the execution component that applies state mutations or external side-effects.

By ensuring that language models and autonomous agents only produce structured, immutable proposals, the system can interpose deterministic acceptance gates, policy validation, and [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) before any irreversible effect occurs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

# Architecture / Specification

## Composition

Under [job-oriented reference architectures](../methodology/job-oriented-reference-architectures.md), the Proposal/Execution Split serves as a foundation for multiple composite workflows:
- **Single-Agent Process with Human Approval**: An agent proposes changes, a human reviewer authorizes them across a [durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) boundary, and an external deterministic executor carries out the action [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].
- **Bounded Autonomous Remediation**: An agent iterates inside a bounded convergence loop until an independent deterministic gate verifies the solution, after which an execution engine applies the constrained remediation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

## Core Invariants

1. **No Direct Agent Mutation**: The reasoning agent has zero write access to production endpoints or state stores.
2. **Typed Proposals**: Proposals are emitted as strongly validated, schema-compliant data structures containing expected pre-conditions and diffs.
3. **Deterministic Execution**: The downstream executor executes only verified proposals without invoking further model reasoning during execution.

mutations.rationale: Captures the Deterministic Acceptance Gate workflow pattern from merged Workflows WG pattern specifications.

proposed_concept.title: Deterministic Acceptance Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow design pattern evaluating candidate results against explicit, repeatable checks and declared scope constraints rather than model self-assessment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Deterministic Acceptance Gate pattern establishes an independent verification barrier in agentic workflows to decide whether a candidate result may advance using explicit, repeatable criteria rather than model self-assessment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]. In bounded autonomous tasks, relying on the generating model to judge its own output risks confident but erroneous self-validation. The gate decouples candidate evaluation into reproducible technical checks, schema validation, contract tests, and task scope enforcement [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification
The gate operates at the boundary between candidate artifact production and workflow state progression [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

Key architectural components include:
- **Deterministic Evaluator**: Executes explicit checks (such as unit test suites, JSON Schema validators, or status checks) against the candidate artifact [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Policy/Scope Validator**: Confirms that candidate outputs do not exceed declared boundaries, including permitted target systems, allowed tool actions, data access boundaries, and maximum permissible impact [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Evidence Store**: Persists cryptographic digests, check inputs, validation logs, and acceptance timestamps bound to the exact candidate version evaluated [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

### Core Invariants
Implementations must preserve several fundamental invariants [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]:
1. Acceptance criteria must be declared prior to candidate evaluation.
2. The gate evaluation mechanism must remain completely independent of the model or agent that produced the candidate result.
3. Acceptance evidence must be bound to the exact candidate artifact digest or version.
4. Passing technical checks is insufficient if task policy or scope validation fails.
5. Missing, failed, or ambiguous gate evaluations must default to fail-closed behavior (non-acceptance).
6. The gate's authority is constrained to its declared scope; downstream actions with higher blast radius require separate authorization controls.

### Interaction with Other Patterns
The Deterministic Acceptance Gate is commonly used in conjunction with the [Bounded Convergence Loop](bounded-convergence-loop.md) to govern iteration exit conditions, and the [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md) to separate proposal verification from workflow execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

mutations.rationale: Captures the Bounded Convergence Loop workflow pattern from merged Workflows WG pattern specifications.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Convergence Loop
proposed_concept.description: Workflow design pattern safely iterating agent tasks within explicit budget and scope constraints until verified by a deterministic gate or terminating in a defined non-success state.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Bounded Convergence Loop pattern governs iterative, agent-assisted problem solving by enforcing explicit scope limits, strict execution budgets, and independent gate evaluation on each cycle [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]. Bounded tasks—such as automated code linting, type correction, or patch remediation—often require multiple diagnostic and editing attempts. This pattern enables multi-step refinement while preventing open-ended iteration, runaway financial costs, and unauthorized autonomous drift [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

# Architecture / Specification
The workflow admits a single bounded task and restricts the agent's tool access and operational scope [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]. Each iteration follows a structured sequence:
1. The agent attempts permitted modifications within its restricted sandbox.
2. An external [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) evaluates the resulting candidate against pre-declared acceptance criteria and scope boundaries.
3. If the gate accepts the candidate, the workflow transitions to controlled downstream execution or a [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md).
4. If the gate rejects the candidate or verification fails, the workflow evaluates configured retry criteria against remaining iteration, time, and cost budgets.
5. If budgets are exhausted or non-retryable errors occur, execution terminates safely in escalation, abstention, or recorded failure [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

### Invariants
To prevent runaway loops and state inconsistency, implementations must enforce the following invariants [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]:
- Scope, tool allowances, and acceptance criteria must be fixed before the loop begins.
- The agent cannot declare convergence or self-certify completion.
- Every retry consumes explicit, non-resettable budget limits (at minimum an iteration count limit and a time or cost threshold).
- Workflow engines must record attempt numbers, gate outcomes, and retry rationales in durable state.
- After an engine interruption or restart, the loop must resume from recorded state without resetting attempt counters or budget limits.

mutations.rationale: Creates the core workflow vocabulary concept establishing foundational terms, execution properties, and coordination models from the Workflows WG.

proposed_concept.title: Core Workflow Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary and foundational concepts defining activities, workflow execution, control flow, durability, and coordination models across AAIF workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Core Workflow Terms define the shared vocabulary for agentic AI workflow models developed by the AAIF [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]. This vocabulary establishes standard definitions for activities, execution lifecycles, durability, determinism, and multi-agent coordination patterns across reference architectures and specifications [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].

# Architecture / Specification
The vocabulary is structured into core ontological layers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]:

### Foundational Concepts
- **Activity**: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31].
- **Workflow**: The primary unit of structured, multi-activity work with a defined goal and outcome, composed of one or more activities and their execution logic [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Execution**: A runtime instance of a workflow definition maintaining its own isolated execution state and lifecycle [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow State**: Information capturing the condition and progress of a workflow execution at a specific point in time [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Workflow Context**: Shared metadata, inputs, execution history, and references available across activities and workflow boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

### Execution & Control
- **Control Flow**: Logic governing execution ordering, branching, parallelism, and synchronization of activities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Durability**: The ability of a workflow execution to persist state across interruptions or failures and resume without losing progress [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Determinism**: The property whereby a workflow produces consistent behavior given identical inputs, state, and history [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

### Coordination Models
- **Orchestration**: Centralized control where a primary workflow coordinator directs activity sequencing and data flow [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Choreography**: Decentralized coordination where autonomous participants interact based on shared protocols and events [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].
- **Composition**: Combining distinct workflows or activities into higher-order workflow units [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f].

proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill for reviewing, categorizing, and triaging community intake submissions across organizer, host, and speaker pipelines.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-triage-intake` skill is an operational community workflow agent skill that processes and triages participant applications submitted through the AAIF Community intake form [^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14]. It acts as a human-in-the-loop review mechanism on top of the automated routing sheet that populates organizer, host, and speaker pipelines.

# Architecture / Specification
The skill manages intake records through an explicit status progression and evaluation model [^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14]:

- **Status Lifecycle**: Applications flow through `Prospect` (or legacy `New`) → `In progress` → `Tentative` (vetted candidate awaiting interview or chapter champion introduction) → `Interviewing` → `Accepted` or `Denied`. Additional terminal or lateral states include `Inactive`, `Existing (from MLOps)`, and `Duplicate` [^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].
- **Duplicate Handling Rules**: A `Duplicate` marker is reserved strictly for identical repeat submissions by the same applicant. Tooling and reviewers must distinguish duplicate records from legitimate multi-role applications (such as an individual applying as both an organizer and a speaker) or multi-pitch submissions (such as multiple distinct talk proposals from one speaker) [^evt-community-events-pr-35].
- **Override Conditions**: Explicit visual and workflow overrides highlight data errors (such as broken LinkedIn profiles or invalid email addresses) and service level agreement (SLA) breaches requiring immediate attention [^evt-community-events-file-55b9c4993977-0d0a7f14].

# References
- Associated event tooling: `../methodology/aaif-clean-data-skill.md`
- Community intake automation: `../project/submission-analyser.md`

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications and reference architectures across autonomous commercial interactions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group standardizes, aligns, and develops reference architectures and open specifications for autonomous AI commerce, transaction lifecycles, negotiation, and settlement.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its core outputs into key deliverables:

- **Capability Map (Deliverable 1)**: Maps end-to-end commercial interaction capabilities across pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase lifecycle phases [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Post-Purchase Capabilities (P1–P7)**: Proposed functional areas covering eligibility inquiry, remedy offer and negotiation, buyer authorization and consent evidence, state-change execution signals, evidence binding, dispute and claims initiation, and adjustment ledgers [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Evidence and Auditability Contract**: Employs an 8-field bounded verdict envelope (`verdict`, `verifier`, `verifier_signature`, `evidence_refs`, `evidence_fingerprints`, `verification_basis`, `witness_scope`, `timestamp`) to ensure verifiable, machine-readable post-transaction settlement across systems [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- **Gap Analysis (Deliverable 2)**: Identifies gaps in existing commercial protocols (such as UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402) and aligns requirements with sibling foundation groups.

# Cross-Working-Group Alignment
- Telemetry and evidence records align with `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].
- Agent identity, consent, and verifiable delegation coordinate with `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md` [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Community Pulse Skill
proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill for synthesizing community updates across Slack, Google Drive, Luma calendar, and Git logs into drafted announcements.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-community-pulse` skill is an operational workflow designed to draft periodic "AAIF Community Organizer Update" announcements for community maintainers and organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-37]. The skill aggregates ecosystem signals from local community channels, intake operations, shared drives, and event platforms while enforcing read-only safety constraints and human authorization before publishing [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates as a proposal-only agent workflow that integrates across multiple upstream community data sources [^evt-community-events-pr-37]:

- **Slack Integration**: Reads recent messages from `#local-champs` via allowlisted read-only methods (`api.ok()`, `api.paged()`) and explicit scope verification [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Drive and Intake Inspection**: Queries the community Chapters Google Drive folder and Intake Ops spreadsheets using Google Workspace CLI tools (`gws`) to detect newly registered chapters and organizers [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Event Tracking**: Scrapes and inspects the Luma calendar for event milestones, attendance wins, and scheduled upcoming community sessions [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Repository Changes**: Computes `git log` diffs across the event operations repository to highlight maintainer-facing procedural changes [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Local Isolation and Security**: Writes temporary organizer data into a restricted `0600` permissions cache within a `0700` directory (`.pulse-cache/`), validating paths against directory traversal and symlink manipulation, and requiring mandatory cache deletion post-generation [^evt-community-events-pr-37].
- **Human Approval Gate**: The skill follows the proposal-execution split pattern and does not post directly to communication channels; it produces drafted update text for review and distribution by human community managers [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

# Lifecycle History
- **PR #37 (community-events)**: Initial implementation and security hardening of the `aaif-community-pulse` skill and Slack reader helper scripts [^evt-community-events-pr-37].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group standardizing agent telemetry models, trace context propagation, cross-agent execution tracing, and security audit schemas.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body established to survey, coordinate, and standardize agent observability, telemetry schemas, and execution tracing across multi-agent ecosystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1]. The group coordinates cross-vendor telemetry alignment across foundational initiatives including OpenTelemetry GenAI, AGNTCY, A2A, and OCSF [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its standardization and landscape analysis around key capability domains [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1]:

- **Prior Work & Ecosystem Tracking**: Maintains an active landscape survey tracking standards such as OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions, OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS), AGNTCY Observe SDK, OCSF Agent Schema, and Agent Trace [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].
- **Trace Model Recommendations**: Evaluates candidate telemetry representations across execution spans, agentic workflow lifecycles, and tool invocations to define adopt/extend/new specification paths [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].
- **Cross-Agent Trace Propagation**: Harmonizes distributed tracing conventions across agent-to-agent communication protocols (e.g., A2A and Model Context Protocol) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].
- **Security and Governance Observability**: Bridges runtime trace telemetry with verifiable security audit schemas, incorporating eBPF/OBI environment telemetry and OCSF identity delegation records [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-03**: Initial landscape survey drafted evaluating prior work across 20+ observability formats and implementations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1].
- **2026-08**: Landscape refreshed with OpenTelemetry GenAI repository split, OCSF 1.9 agent profile, and AGNTCY Observe updates [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-5a4323f1]. Contributor onboarding guidelines and Trace Model recommendation planning initiated [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-17][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync-badges` skill generates chapter organizer badge assets (SVG vectors and rendered PNGs) and synchronizes them to the canonical AAIF community Google Drive repository [^evt-community-events-pr-38]. It scans canonical chapter listings, identifies missing badges using an additive diff calculation, and uploads missing graphic assets [^evt-community-events-pr-38].

# Architecture / Specification
The badge synchronization workflow consists of two core components [^evt-community-events-pr-38]:
- `make_badges.py`: Renders ring/arc badge SVGs with XML-escaped chapter titles and rasterizes them to 1000px PNGs using `cairosvg` [^evt-community-events-pr-38].
- `sync_badges.py`: Interfaces with the Google Workspace CLI (`gws`) to list Chapter directories, compare existing badge assets, and upload missing files [^evt-community-events-pr-38]. Runs in dry-run plan mode by default and provides `--write`, `--regenerate`, and `--chapter` operational flags [^evt-community-events-pr-38].

# References
- [AAIF Community Events PR #38](https://github.com/aaif/community-events/pull/38)

mutations.rationale: This event defines a new reference architecture for workflows requiring human authorization before executing protected effects.

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture ensuring protected effects only occur after explicit human authorization of an agent-generated proposal.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
This reference architecture defines the structure for a common enterprise job: an agent prepares an action, a named human approves or rejects it, and only then may the protected effect occur [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

It is used when an agent's output can change real systems (e.g., a refund, configuration change, or outbound message) and the enterprise requires enforceable behavior at the point of effect due to cost, reversibility, audit obligations, or ownership requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

# Architecture / Specification
This architecture places a human-mediated structural break between the agent's proposal and the protected effect. The agent may investigate and construct a proposal, but a separate, workflow-controlled executor acts only after recording explicit human approval [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

The architecture guarantees three invariants:
1. No protected effect occurs without human approval, and what executes is exactly what was approved.
2. The run survives the wait (approvals may take hours or days).
3. Every run ends in a known state, with the full intent → decision → effect chain recorded in the system of record.

It is built from the following patterns:
*   [Proposal/execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
*   [Human approval gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
*   [Durable wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md)

Required capabilities include an execution engine, agent, tool access layer, state/context store, human interaction surface, workflow-controlled executor, and audit log [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-4ea33af5].

proposed_concept.description: Operational agent skill for generating and synchronizing AAIF chapter organizer badge assets in Google Drive, handling two distinct badge styles and rendering methods.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `aaif-sync-badges` skill is an operational agent capability used to synchronize AAIF chapter organizer badges (SVG and PNG formats) into each chapter's dedicated Drive folder. It can generate missing badges or optionally regenerate all badges following a design change [^evt-community-events-file-777711ce3f1c-7d1a1733].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill operates using `gws` (Google Workspace CLI) and Python, strictly preferring native Google formats and avoiding tools like LibreOffice or `unoconv` to ensure accurate representation of brand assets [^evt-community-events-file-777711ce3f1c-7d1a1733].

The skill manages six files per chapter, representing two distinct badge styles stored in a `Badges/` subfolder:

1.  **`make_badges.py` style:** A ring-and-arc badge using a self-contained, hand-tuned palette and system font stack. This style is rendered to PNG via `cairosvg` [^evt-community-events-file-777711ce3f1c-7d1a1733].
2.  **`make_agent_badge.py` style:** Draws from the official AAIF design system, including the chapter's specific agent mascot. This variant is rendered via headless Chrome to ensure provable adherence to the design system [^evt-community-events-file-777711ce3f1c-7d1a1733].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group (S&P WG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the Agentic AI ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-a40a890b].

The group produces open threat models, a shared taxonomy, and design patterns that providers, consumers, and peer working groups can adopt to share responsibility for trustworthy agentic AI [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-a40a890b].

# Lifecycle History
The WG meets biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-a40a890b].

**Chairs:**
*   Chair: Alex Frazer (Runlayer)
*   Co-Chair: Junjie Bu (Google)

The current term for the chairs is March 1, 2026 - January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-a40a890b].

The WG manages several active workstreams:
*   [Best Practices](../working-groups/sp-best-practices.md)
*   [Design Patterns](../working-groups/sp-design-patterns.md)
*   [Review Checklist](../working-groups/sp-review-checklist.md)
*   [Threat Modeling](../working-groups/sp-threat-modeling.md)
*   Taxonomy and Landscape (cross-WG initiative) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]

# Overview
This workstream is responsible for developing the Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide, providing practical guidance, guardrails, and secrets management recommendations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History
The first version of the best practices document was frozen and merged in early September 2026, marking its transition into the WG's formal deliverable process (publish, socialize internally, then promote publicly) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

Identity and trust topics were explicitly excluded from this initial version, pending ownership discussions with the Identity and Trust WG [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

A parallel effort is underway to convert the security best practices into actionable rules usable by static analysis tools, creating a code-facing deliverable alongside the document [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Action Capsule is a proposed specification designed to serve as a middle layer between regulations and agent actions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

It records key information about an agent's operation: what was dispatched, what happened, and whether the action was allowed to happen. This mechanism is intended to prevent tampering through the use of cryptographic proofs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Architecture / Specification
The capsule enables verification and reconstruction of complete execution traces from multiple capsules via a ledger system. It is being explored for integration with existing traceability and observability efforts, particularly within the Observability and Traceability Working Group [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group (WG Government, Risk & Regulatory Alignment) is an AAIF working group chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase)[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]. The group bridges global policy developments, legislation, and industry standards with technical specifications for agentic AI systems.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's charter deliverables follow a three-phase progression[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a]:

1. **Phase 1: Landscape Analysis**: Identifying and cataloging relevant policy instruments, legislative frameworks, and best practices across global jurisdictions.
2. **Phase 2: Thematic Mapping and Gap Analysis**: Mapping policy instruments against approximately a dozen common governance and risk themes, developing AI prompt workflows for consistent extraction, and synthesizing gap analysis findings.
3. **Phase 3: Recommendations and Final Deliverable**: Publishing technical alignment recommendations and guidance for AAIF working groups and member organizations.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07**: Completed the initial landscape analysis phase and established consensus on initial policy instruments and thematic categories, commencing Phase 2 gap analysis mapping[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a].

# References

- Charter and monthly reporting in `aaif/wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory`[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-fa4050a9f626-ee69c81a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-7].
- Cross-references: [../governance/technical-committee.md](../governance/technical-committee.md), [../governance/working-group-reporting.md](../governance/working-group-reporting.md).

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture ensuring protected actions only execute following explicit human review and authorization of immutable proposals.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Single-Agent Human Approval Reference Architecture defines patterns and execution boundaries where an autonomous agent proposes actions or content modifications, but protected execution or publication only occurs after explicit human authorization[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36].

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture establishes three distinct operational boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]:

1. **Proposal Generation**: The agent operates autonomously within its tools and context to assemble candidate changes or artifacts (such as draft documentation or copy), emitted as an immutable proposal.
2. **Human Approval Gate**: The proposal is held in a durable waiting state, presented to an authorized human principal via an explicit approval interface.
3. **Publication / Execution Boundary**: Upon verified authorization by the human reviewer, a deterministic execution engine applies or publishes the changes.

## Validated Scenarios

The Workflows and Process Integration WG validates this architecture against standard content operational use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]:
- **FAQ and Knowledge Base Updates**: Drafting and validating edits to internal and public knowledge repositories before publication.
- **Release Notes Generation**: Synthesizing software changelogs and pull request histories into customer-facing release notes.
- **Listing and Catalog Descriptions**: Generating and updating marketplace listing metadata subject to editorial review.

# References

- Cross-references: [../patterns/human-approval-gate.md](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), [../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), [../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md).

proposed_concept.title: Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Design system specifications, typography rules, color tokens, and asset usage policies for AAIF visual identities and community reports.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF design system establishes strict visual identity standards for all generated collateral, community reports, dashboards, and official communications[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. All materials must conform to centralized design tokens rather than ad-hoc custom styling[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core System Rules
- **Color and Accents**: Primary actions and brand accent default to black (`--accent: var(--ink)`). Spectrum hues (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) serve exclusively as internal surface accents with at most one hue leading at a time (e.g., coral is `--spec-8` rather than a primary brand color)[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. The ground canvas is `--paper`, tinted panels use `--paper-3`, and `--paper-2` is reserved for occasional section banding[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Surfaces**: Visual outputs strictly use two first-class surfaces: white editorial pages and deliberate black plates. Dark-mode theme swapping (`prefers-color-scheme`) is prohibited[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Typography**: Instrument Sans is the singular typeface (weights 400, 500, 600, 700) across display and UI[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]. Headings use weight 500, tracking `-0.02em`, and line-height 1.05–1.15. Monospace fonts are restricted to metadata and eyebrows[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].
- **Geometry & Elevation**: The design language is flat with no drop shadows; hierarchy is achieved via 1px hairlines, surface tinting, and inset strokes. Box corners remain square (`border-radius: 0`), reserving rounded pill styling (`--radius-pill`) solely for actual badge and button elements[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

### Brand Assets and Usage
- **Mark Integrity**: The official vector assets live in `assets/` (`aaif-mark.svg` for full black lockup, `aaif-mark-square.svg` for square mark avatars/favicons, and `aaif-logo-white.svg` for black plates)[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07][^evt-community-events-pr-41]. Redrawing the mark from memory, screenshots, or unapproved approximations is forbidden[^evt-community-events-pr-41].
- **Agent Motif**: The agent motif constructed from mark primitives may only appear on empty states, loading screens, event graphics, and visual dividers—never on governance, board, or press material[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07].

# References
- [Design System Specification](https://github.com/aaif/community-events/blob/main/DESIGN.md)[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Core Workflow Terms define the structural primitives and architectural concepts underpinning workflow design and process integration within the AAIF[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

# Architecture / Specification

### Defined Terms and Layering Semantics
- **Determinism**: Evaluated as a property of a specific execution layer—such as Workflow Execution, Control Flow, or an individual Activity—rather than an all-or-nothing property of an entire composite workflow[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]. This allows workflows with deterministic control flow to incorporate non-deterministic agentic activities without semantic contradiction[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Control Flow**: The logic that determines execution order, branching, and routing. The definition remains agnostic to whether sequencing is statically fixed at design time or evaluated dynamically by an agent at runtime, deferring agent coordination mechanics to Orchestration[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Workflow Execution**: The end-to-end lifecycle of execution states and transitions from initiation to completion. Execution identity persists across dynamic mid-execution replanning or retry events[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].
- **Handoff**: Characterized by complementary viewpoints across working groups: the delegation and transfer of operational responsibility, and the observable telemetry boundary where the transfer occurs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40].

# References
- [Refining Determinism, Control Flow, Workflow Execution, and Handoff](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/pull/40)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-40]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Framework
proposed_concept.description: Structural five-dimension classification framework for standardizing agentic workflows, HITL oversight patterns, and autonomy graduation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification framework categorizes agentic workflows across operational dimensions, human-in-the-loop (HITL) patterns, and lifecycle autonomy progression[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# Architecture / Specification

### HITL Oversight Patterns
- **Approval Gate**: Intermittent verification checkpoints utilized while confidence in autonomous execution is being established[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
- **Exception Escalation**: Execution proceeds autonomously unless specific anomaly or confidence thresholds trigger human intervention[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
- **Hard Constraint**: Non-negotiable, permanent human oversight mandated by external regulation, legal certifications, or governance policy (such as physician signatures or board expenditure approvals) rather than system confidence limitations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

### Autonomy Graduation
Systems may evolve along an operational graduation path over time as trust and validation mature (progressing from `Approval gate` to `Exception escalation` to `None`). In contrast, workflows classified under `Hard constraint` are permanently barred from autonomy graduation due to non-negotiable statutory or institutional compliance requirements[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# References
- [HITL Hard Constraints and Autonomy Graduation](https://github.com/aaif/wg-workflows-and-process-integration/pull/42)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and viewpoints for agent identity, attestation, authentication, and delegated authority.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group advancing vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Its mission is to enable agents to be discovered across platforms, verify their provenance and human authority, operate securely across organizational boundaries, and produce auditable traces of human approval [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its activities across three specialized breakout groups that coordinate with the main working group cadence [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Use Cases Breakout** (coordinated by Wei Chen): Grounds requirements in enterprise and consumer agent scenarios and authority flows [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Reference Architecture Breakout** (coordinated by Brian Malone): Maps actors, trust domains, component relationships, and delegation gaps [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Taxonomy Coordination** (liaisons Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky): Harmonizes identity terminology with the cross-working-group [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

The group evaluates external technical foundations and reference works including SPIFFE/SPIRE workload attestation, the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification, Uber's agent identity and token exchange architecture, NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace reference design, and IETF AI agent authentication and authorization internet drafts [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Governance and Operations
- **Leadership**: Chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and co-chaired by Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE) for the March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 term [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].
- **Cadence**: Public meetings occur every Thursday, alternating weekly between 6:30 AM PT and 9:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].
- **Tracking and Agendas**: Meeting notes, AI summaries, and recordings are archived via LFX and Google Docs, while unallocated proposals and presentation topics are tracked in the outstanding agenda queue [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3] [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-c743b929b22e-3767aad0].
- **Collaboration**: Public communication is hosted on the `wg-identity-trust` mailing list and dedicated AAIF Discord channels under Linux Foundation antitrust and neutrality commitments [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].

mutations.rationale: Create reference architecture concept capturing cross-boundary observability, trace context propagation, and lifecycle guarantees across the Agent-to-Tool local CLI process boundary.

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Observability
proposed_concept.description: Cross-boundary observability architecture and telemetry propagation model for agent runtimes invoking finite local CLI subprocesses directly.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary reference architecture defines the telemetry model, context propagation mechanisms, and causality guarantees required when an AI agent runtime directly launches a local Command Line Interface (CLI) subprocess as a tool [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. Formulated within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), it distinguishes between the semantic Agent → Tool decision boundary and the operational Agent Runtime → Local Process launch boundary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Architecture / Specification
The boundary spans two interacting surfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
1. **Agent Execution Surface**: Where the model selects a tool, produces a tool call identifier (`gen_ai.tool.call.id`), and supplies structured arguments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
2. **Operating System Process Surface**: Where the runtime resolves the binary path, sets up environment variables, launches the child process, monitors its lifecycle, and captures its outcome [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

### Trace Propagation and Carriers
Because local CLI subprocesses lack network transport headers, causal context must cross into the child process at invocation time via environment-variable carriers before process start [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. Reconstructing tool calls retrospectively from post-execution transcripts breaks real-time child instrumentation and prevents child spans from correctly declaring the parent tool span [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

The architecture evaluates field coverage and gaps across six primary observability dimensions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
- **Identity**: Combines OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.tool.name` and `gen_ai.tool.call.id` with process PID and executable path, highlighting open gaps in binding executable digests and delegation principal identities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Context**: Relies on W3C Trace Context and Baggage propagated via OpenTelemetry environment-variable carrier specifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Relationship**: Maintains causal hierarchy between governing agent turns, tool spans, and local child execution spans, using span links for asynchronous or detached background jobs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Lifecycle**: Tracks state transitions across selection, authorization, environment preparation, process spawning, active execution, and termination/cancellation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Outcome**: Captures exit codes (`process.exit.code`), structured tool outputs, and error classifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Provenance**: Records the tool declaration origin, runtime plugin, resolved binary path, and telemetry observer metadata [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Lifecycle History
The deep dive was developed in the Observability and Traceability WG (facilitated by `@fangxiu-wf` under Issue #29) and incorporates reference implementation validations from LoongSuite Pilot and Claude Code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Structural classification framework and evidentiary methodology for cataloging production agentic workflows and orchestration patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Agentic Use Case Classification framework is a structured methodology maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to identify, categorize, and catalog reusable workflow patterns extracted from real-world agentic systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]. The framework combines a standardized multi-dimensional schema with a strictly sourced use case inventory [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

# Architecture / Specification

### Evidentiary Standards

The framework enforces strict evidentiary standards to ensure cataloged workflows reflect actual production architectures rather than aspirational vendor messaging [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]:

- **Primary Source Grounding**: Every inventory row must cite primary vendor documentation, engineering publications, or official deployment announcements verifying confirmed production operation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Citation Thresholds**: A minimum of one verified primary citation is required per entry, with three independent citations targeted [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].
- **Execution Substantiation**: Classification values (such as sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out, or convergence loops) must be directly supported by architectural descriptions in cited sources [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].
- **Explicit Ambiguity Handling**: If cited sources do not explicitly describe execution ordering, concurrency, or coordination mechanisms, the corresponding attributes must remain designated as unspecified [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

### Core Workstream Artifacts

- `schema-agentic-use-cases.md`: Canonical schema defining classification dimensions, valid categorical values, and row classification rules [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-48].
- `use-case-inventory.md`: The verified inventory of production use cases mapped across coordination, human oversight, and orchestration dimensions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-39].

# Lifecycle History

Developed under the Critical Use Cases workstream within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46].

proposed_concept.title: Meta-harness
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy definition and scope note for meta-harnesses orchestrating and composing lower-level agent execution harnesses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A meta-harness is an architectural construct and execution framework that composes, coordinates, or manages multiple specialized agent harnesses across workflow stages [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48]. Standardized by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the term distinguishes higher-level coordination layers from individual, low-level execution harnesses [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].

# Architecture / Specification
In the AAIF SKOS Lite taxonomy model, `Meta-harness` is linked to `Harness` through bidirectional `relatedTerms` relationships rather than strict hierarchy or contrast, reflecting their compositional nature [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48]:
- **Compositional Relationship**: A meta-harness acts above single-agent harnesses, orchestrating multiple runtimes or tool-boundary environments rather than replacing individual runtime harnesses [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].
- **Taxonomy Placement**: Categorized alongside agent execution models and runtime architectures to unify vocabulary across AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48].

# References
- AAIF Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-48]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Human curated is an AAIF taxonomy term designating artifacts, catalog entries, or landscape datasets that have undergone explicit manual review and verification by human domain experts [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39]. Maintained by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), the designation serves as an assurance signal distinguishing human-reviewed items from unverified or automated outputs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39].

# Architecture / Specification
The definition and scope note specify criteria for quality assurance within AAIF catalogs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39]:
- **Assurance Signal**: Confirms that entries reflect human validation of claims, capabilities, and classifications rather than unverified third-party scraping or automated generation [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39].
- **Taxonomy Integration**: Included in the taxonomy schema to standardize metadata attributes across AAIF landscape projects [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39].

# References
- AAIF Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-39]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification
proposed_concept.description: Classification framework and evidentiary methodology for cataloging production agentic workflows and multi-agent coordination patterns.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification framework is a structured methodology maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to catalog, classify, and analyze real-world production agentic workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]. It provides a standardized schema for documenting human-in-the-loop (HITL) patterns, orchestration topologies, and empirical evidence from verified industry deployments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# Architecture / Specification

## Evidentiary Standards
Use case catalog entries must adhere to primary source validation requirements to prevent unverified claims and maintain empirical rigor [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **Preferred Evidence**: Official vendor product documentation or announcements demonstrating named customer production deployments operating at scale [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Acceptable Evidence**: Vendor product pages detailing concrete production capabilities even in the absence of named customer attribution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Unacceptable Sources**: Secondary blog posts, analyst commentary, speculative market projections, academic preprints, or individual implementer write-ups [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Citation Density & Health**: Inventory rows target three verified primary citations, tracking dates and managing link rot risks [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

## Structural Classification Fields
The framework evaluates workflows along defined coordination and execution dimensions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **HITL & Approval Gates**: Standardized classification of oversight mechanisms such as [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and deterministic review steps [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Multi-Agent Rationale**: Explicit architectural justification for classifying workflows as *Better as multi-agent* versus *Inherently multi-agent* [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].
- **Coordination Alignment**: Mappings to standard patterns described in [agentic-workflow-orchestration-patterns](../methodology/agentic-workflow-orchestration-patterns.md) and [workflow-design-specification](../methodology/workflow-design-specification.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

# References
- AAIF Workflows and Process Integration Working Group [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation, responsible for overseeing technical standards, best practices, and the overarching technical vision across the foundation [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]. The TC operates under the Technical Charter established by the AAIF Governing Board and oversees foundation working groups, review procedures, and project lifecycle transitions [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Architecture / Specification

## Membership and Leadership
All founding Technical Committee members are appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for the term spanning March 1, 2026 to December 31, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:
- **David Soria Parra** (Anthropic) – TC Chair
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Microsoft) – TC Co-Chair
- **Alan Blount** (Google)
- **Bradley Axen** (Block)
- **James Ward** (Amazon Web Services)
- **Nick Cooper** (OpenAI)
- **Sambhav Kothari** (Bloomberg)
- **Steve Faulkner** (Cloudflare)

## Project Oversight and Stages
The TC evaluates candidate and hosted projects against the [Project Lifecycle](../governance/project-lifecycle.md) criteria. Flagship projects accepted into the foundation's Impact Stage include:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: Open protocol enabling seamless integration between LLM applications, external data sources, and tools [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].
- **goose**: Open-source, extensible AI agent runtime executing and testing tasks across arbitrary LLMs [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].
- **AGENTS.MD**: Specification and convention tooling for agent context and runtime discovery [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# References
- [Project Proposal Process](../governance/project-proposal-process.md)
- [Working Group Submission Guidelines](../governance/wg-submission-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.title: Human in the Loop (HITL)
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy standard defining synchronous human intervention checkpoints required before an agent executes protected actions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Human in the Loop (HITL) is an accepted Agentic AI Foundation taxonomy term specifying an operational architecture and control requirement where an agent workflow halts at defined checkpoints, requiring active human authorization or review before proceeding [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Semantic Boundaries
Within the AAIF Taxonomy framework, Human in the Loop is delineated from related control patterns [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40]:
- **Human in the Loop (HITL)**: Requires synchronous human intervention and explicit review at an enforcement barrier prior to task completion or sensitive state transitions [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40]. See [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
- **Human on the Loop (HOTL)**: Involves asynchronous monitoring and supervisory control where the human oversees autonomous agent execution and intervenes only for exceptions or policy deviations [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40].
- **Handoff**: Represents an operational transfer of execution control where the agent permanently or conditionally yields the active task execution context to a human operator or secondary agent system [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-40].

# References
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Single-Agent Human Approval Reference Architecture](../reference-architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md)
- [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md)

mutations.rationale: Add agreed Identity & Trust taxonomy definitions for Trust, Identifier, Attestation, and Delegation from the Taxonomy and Landscape workstream.

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Taxonomy Terms
proposed_concept.description: Standardized taxonomy vocabulary defining Trust, Identifier, Attestation, and Delegation across agentic architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust taxonomy vocabulary provides formal terminology agreed upon by the AAIF Taxonomy and Landscape workstream in alignment with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42]. It establishes explicit definitions for foundational security primitives across agent ecosystems.

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Terminology
The taxonomy defines four primary concepts under the Identity & Trust category [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42]:

1. **Trust**: The verifiable expectation that an agent, runtime component, or service will execute in alignment with specified behavioral policies, security constraints, and operational bounds [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42].
2. **Identifier**: A globally or locally unique, stable token or URI assigned to an agent, principal, tool, or resource to disambiguate entities during interaction and authorization flows [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42].
3. **Attestation**: Cryptographic or cryptographically verifiable evidence asserting the identity, integrity, execution state, or configuration of an agent or runtime environment [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42]. Related to [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).
4. **Delegation**: The formal mechanism by which an entity (human user or agent) confers scoped authority or permissions to another agent to perform operations on its behalf [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42]. Delegation links directly to runtime execution handoffs [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-42].

# References
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)
- [Core Workflow Terms](../taxonomy/core-workflow-terms.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Framework
proposed_concept.description: Classification framework and evidentiary methodology for cataloging production agentic workflows and execution structures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification Framework provides structured criteria for inventorying, classifying, and comparing real-world agentic workflows developed across industry sectors [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]. Curated by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), it maps workflow topology, coordination patterns, autonomy levels, and validation mechanics into standardized schema fields.

# Architecture / Specification

## Topology and Execution Dimensions
The schema evaluates agentic use cases across structural execution dimensions:
- **Workflow Pattern Type**: Distinguishes sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out orchestrations, routing networks, and autonomous loops.
- **Autonomy and Human Control**: Classifies interaction models across automated, human-in-the-loop, and supervisory topologies.
- **Artifact and State Handoff**: Captures how state, prompts, tool outputs, and context transfer between participating agents.

## Open Architectural Debates
An ongoing discussion in the use case classification schema addresses ambiguous boundaries between `Parallel fan-out` (defined by concurrent sub-task timing) and `Sequential pipeline` (defined by activity dependencies where each step feeds the next) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]. Working group members are evaluating three candidate classification interpretations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-47]:
1. **Observed Timing**: Classifying based strictly on whether execution occurs concurrently or sequentially in time.
2. **Agent / Worker Count**: Distinguishing based on whether single or multi-agent instances participate concurrently.
3. **Data and Activity Dependency**: Classifying based solely on dependency graphs and state handoff topologies regardless of runtime concurrency.

# References
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)
- [Agentic Workflow Orchestration Patterns](../methodology/agentic-workflow-orchestration-patterns.md)
- [Job-Oriented Reference Architectures](../methodology/job-oriented-reference-architectures.md)

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Methodology
proposed_concept.description: Evaluation framework and review workflow for assessing the architectural fit of reference architectures against documented use cases.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Reference Architecture (RA) Use-Case Validation Methodology provides a standardized procedure for evaluating whether a proposed or existing Reference Architecture fits a verified production agentic use case[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. Established by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), this methodology allows human contributors and autonomous coding agents to test architectural alignment without requiring an existing codebase to fully implement every technical control upfront[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Architecture / Specification

## Validation Scope and Core Principle

Validation assesses whether a target use case shares the primary operational job and defining boundaries addressed by the reference architecture[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

- **Architectural Fit vs. Implementation Conformance**: A `Validated` classification indicates that the reference architecture provides the appropriate structural roles, boundaries, and failure controls for the job[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. It does not certify that a specific running deployment already complies with all reference architecture mechanisms (such as retry parameters, token storage, or credential handling)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Evidentiary Standard**: Evaluations must rely strictly on documented facts in the Use Case Inventory or cited primary sources, rather than synthetic examples or illustrative scenarios within pattern templates[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

## Evaluation Workflow

1. **Boundary and Responsibility Mapping**: Inspect who executes each task across agent, orchestrator/workflow engine, human operator, and external systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
2. **Check Definition**: Construct two or three targeted validation checks addressing the core job and required boundaries; do not mandate evidence for omitted low-level implementation details unless they alter architectural fit[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
3. **Result Classification**: Assign one of four standardized status values[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35]:
   - `Validated`: Strong architectural alignment with the main job and boundaries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
   - `Partial`: Fits core elements but exhibits significant boundary mismatches or missing failure handling[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
   - `No fit`: The use case requires a fundamentally different coordination pattern or job structure[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
   - `Candidate`: Insufficient factual evidence available to determine architectural fit[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

## Contribution Output

Findings are submitted as either a lightweight GitHub Issue (when seeking consensus on ambiguous boundaries) or a direct pull request appending the validation record to the Reference Architecture document[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

# Lifecycle History

Introduced in PR #35 following Reference Architecture Workstream Sync #6 to provide consistent guidelines for validating architectural models across practitioner use cases[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

proposed_concept.title: Job-Oriented Workflow Reference Architectures
proposed_concept.description: Framework organizing workflow reference architectures around practitioner operational jobs, reusable patterns, and validation scenarios.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Job-Oriented Reference Architecture model is an architectural framework curated by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) that organizes workflow reference architectures around concrete practitioner jobs rather than generic product categories or isolated technical mechanisms[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. The methodology establishes strict differentiation between atomic patterns, multi-pattern reference architectures, validation scenarios, and decision records[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Architecture / Specification

## Structural Taxonomy

The framework establishes explicit structural roles across three primary contribution types[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]:

| Contribution Type | Granularity | Scope and Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Pattern** | Sub-problem | Solves one recurring workflow challenge (such as [durable-wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md) or [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)) independently of specific end-to-end jobs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. |
| **Reference Architecture** | Practitioner Job | Defines the complete logical composition, capability boundaries, execution guarantees, and exit states answering *"We are building a [Job]"*[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4]. |
| **Scenario** | Instance/Evidence | A concrete or illustrative workflow example used in validation records to test architectural fit; scenarios do not constitute standalone architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30]. |

## Authoring and Contribution Rules

Contributors (including autonomous AI coding agents) must adhere to mandatory authoring principles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30]:

- **Vendor Neutrality**: Specify capabilities and required invariants at the logical role level before referencing concrete vendor products or implementations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].
- **Boundary Clarity**: Explicitly delineate what is controlled by the non-deterministic agent versus deterministic workflow orchestrators and human operators[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].
- **Evidence vs. Interpretation**: Distinguish empirically verified facts from proposed working group interpretations, maintaining genuine gaps as explicit open questions[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].
- **Validation Coupling**: Every reference architecture is linked to real-world use cases using the [reference-architecture-validation methodology](../methodology/reference-architecture-validation.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

# Lifecycle History

Adopted in the `workstreams/reference-architectures` directory of the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group as the standard structure for curating patterns, architectures, and use case validation guides[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture enabling autonomous iteration and bounded remediation under independent deterministic acceptance gates and constrained effects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a reference architecture designed to resolve discrete, bounded problems autonomously using independent deterministic acceptance evidence and safe escalation when tasks fail to converge [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. It serves operational jobs where human approval is not required for every attempt, provided the task operates within explicit scope, tool, and budget boundaries and produces a low-impact or reversible effect [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

The architecture contrasts with [single-agent-human-approval](single-agent-human-approval.md) by substituting named human review with an automated, independent deterministic gate when verifiable criteria exist [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is composed from three core workflow patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- [Bounded convergence loop](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md): Iterates agent remediation attempts within explicit budget, credential, and tool limits.
- [Deterministic acceptance gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md): Validates candidate work against test suites, contracts, schemas, or policy rules prior to effect execution.
- [Proposal/execution split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Isolates candidate outputs in non-authoritative work areas until verified.

Key architectural guarantees include [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]:
- **Bounded autonomy:** The agent operates strictly with predefined task scope, sandboxed data, and resource budgets.
- **Independent acceptance:** Candidate results are evaluated by an external deterministic acceptance gate rather than self-assessed by the agent.
- **Controlled effect:** Only verified, scope-conforming changes are applied by a dedicated effect executor.
- **Safe non-convergence:** Any non-converging execution, budget exhaustion, or ambiguous outcome halts in an explicit state and escalates to human-operated queues.

# Lifecycle History
The Bounded Autonomous Remediation reference architecture was developed within the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. Scenarios including autonomous maintenance runs and staff schedule generation were validated to confirm acceptance criteria and boundary requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].
